writer.name: Seneca
writer.bio: Roman Stoic, born in Spain around 4 BC. One of the richest men in Rome, exiled to Corsica for eight years, then tutor and adviser to the emperor Nero. Nero ordered his death in AD 65.

works.title: Moral Letters to Lucilius
works.note: Written in the last three years of his life, after he had pulled back from Nero's court and knew the order to die could come any day. 124 letters to his younger friend Lucilius, meant from the start to be read by others.

works.title: On Providence
works.note: An answer to Lucilius, who had asked why bad things happen to good men if the world is run well. Seneca's reply is that hardship is training.

works.title: On the Constancy of the Wise Man
works.note: Written to his friend Serenus, arguing that a wise man cannot really be injured or insulted, because nothing that matters to him can be taken.

works.title: On Anger
works.note: Three books written for his brother Novatus around AD 41 to 45, not long after the reign of Caligula showed Rome what rage with power behind it looks like.

works.title: On a Happy Life
works.note: Written for his brother Gallio around AD 58, when Seneca was at the height of his wealth and being attacked for preaching simplicity while living rich. Part of it is his answer to that.

works.title: On Leisure
works.note: A fragment on whether a man may step back from public life to think. Written around the time Seneca was trying to leave Nero's court himself.

works.title: On Peace of Mind
works.note: It opens with his friend Serenus describing a restless, unsettled mind and asking for a cure. The rest is Seneca's answer.

works.title: On the Shortness of Life
works.note: Written around AD 49 for Paulinus, the man in charge of Rome's grain supply, telling him to retire. The argument: life is long enough, we just waste most of it.

quotes.text: What man can you show me who places any value on his time, who reckons the worth of each day, who understands that he is dying daily?
quotes.plain: Almost nobody counts their days. You are spending them right now whether you count or not.

quotes.text: Whatever years lie behind us are in death’s hands.
quotes.plain: The past is already gone. All you have is what is left.

quotes.text: Lay hold of to-day’s task, and you will not need to depend so much upon to-morrow’s.
quotes.plain: Do today's work today and tomorrow gets lighter.

quotes.text: While we are postponing, life speeds by.
quotes.plain: Every day you put it off is a day gone for good.

quotes.text: Nothing, Lucilius, is ours, except time.
quotes.plain: Time is the only thing you truly own, so stop letting people and habits spend it for you.

quotes.text: And yet time is the one loan which even a grateful recipient cannot repay.
quotes.plain: You can't pay time back, so treat every hour like it cost you something.

quotes.text: The primary indication, to my thinking, of a well-ordered mind is a man’s ability to remain in one place and linger in his own company.
quotes.plain: A steady mind can sit still alone without needing to escape.

quotes.text: Everywhere means nowhere.
quotes.plain: If you are everywhere at once, you are getting nowhere. Pick one thing and stay.

quotes.text: It is not the man who has too little, but the man who craves more, that is poor.
quotes.plain: Poor is about wanting more, not about how much you have.

quotes.text: Do you ask what is the proper limit to wealth? It is, first, to have what is necessary, and, second, to have what is enough.
quotes.plain: Get what you need, then get what is enough. Past that it is just appetite.

quotes.text: When friendship is settled, you must trust; before friendship is formed, you must pass judgment.
quotes.plain: Vet people first. Once they are in, trust them fully.

quotes.text: It is equally faulty to trust everyone and to trust no one.
quotes.plain: Trusting everybody and trusting nobody are both mistakes.

quotes.text: For love of bustle is not industry, it is only the restlessness of a hunted mind.
quotes.plain: Being busy is not the same as working. Often it is just anxiety in motion.

quotes.text: Boys fear trifles, children fear shadows, we fear both.
quotes.plain: Most of what scares you is small or imaginary, and you are old enough to know better.

quotes.text: No evil is great which is the last evil of all.
quotes.plain: Death ends everything, including the pain, so it cannot be the worst thing.

quotes.text: Most men ebb and flow in wretchedness between the fear of death and the hardships of life; they are unwilling to live, and yet they do not know how to die.
quotes.plain: People dread dying and dread living, and get stuck between the two.

quotes.text: No good thing renders its possessor happy, unless his mind is reconciled to the possibility of loss; nothing, however, is lost with less discomfort than that which, when lost, cannot be missed.
quotes.plain: Enjoy what you have while accepting you could lose it. Needing it less makes losing it hurt less.

quotes.text: No man has ever been so far advanced by Fortune that she did not threaten him as greatly as she had previously indulged him.
quotes.plain: Luck can lift you high, but it can drop you just as far.

quotes.text: Take my word for it: since the day you were born you are being led thither.
quotes.plain: You have been heading toward death since birth. Fearing it now changes nothing.

quotes.text: He who has made a fair compact with poverty is rich.
quotes.plain: If you can be at peace with having little, you are already rich.

quotes.text: It is the sign of an unstable mind not to be able to endure riches.
quotes.plain: Handling money well, without it going to your head, is a test too.

quotes.text: Just as the same chain fastens the prisoner and the soldier who guards him, so hope and fear, dissimilar as they are, keep step together; fear follows hope.
quotes.plain: Hope and fear are chained together. Lean hard on one and you get the other.

quotes.text: Beasts avoid the dangers which they see, and when they have escaped them are free from care; but we men torment ourselves over that which is to come as well as over that which is past.
quotes.plain: Animals face danger once. You suffer it before, during, and after.

quotes.text: The present alone can make no man wretched.
quotes.plain: Right now, this moment, is almost always bearable. The misery lives in past and future.

quotes.text: No good thing is pleasant to possess, without friends to share it.
quotes.plain: Wins feel empty with nobody to share them with.

quotes.text: “What progress, you ask, have I made? I have begun to be a friend to myself.”
quotes.plain: Real progress starts when you stop being your own enemy.

quotes.text: The young character, which cannot hold fast to righteousness, must be rescued from the mob; it is too easy to side with the majority.
quotes.plain: Going along with the crowd is the easy default. Guard against it.

quotes.text: Withdraw into yourself, as far as you can.
quotes.plain: Pull back from the noise. Your head clears when you are not performing for anyone.

quotes.text: “I am content with few, content with one, content with none at all.”
quotes.plain: Be fine with a few people, or none, in your corner.

quotes.text: Many men praise you; but have you any reason for being pleased with yourself, if you are a person whom the many can understand?
quotes.plain: If everybody gets you and likes you, you may not be doing anything hard or original.

quotes.text: Your good qualities should face inwards.
quotes.plain: Build character for yourself, not for the audience.

quotes.text: The body should be treated more rigorously, that it may not be disobedient to the mind.
quotes.plain: Train your body hard so it does what your mind says.

quotes.text: “If you would enjoy real freedom, you must be the slave of Philosophy.”
quotes.plain: Freedom comes from discipline, not from doing whatever you feel like.

quotes.text: Hecato, says: “I can show you a philtre, compounded without drugs, herbs, or any witch’s incantation: ‘If you would be loved, love.’”
quotes.plain: Want to be loved? Show up and love people first.

quotes.text: He who begins to be your friend because it pays will also cease because it pays.
quotes.plain: People who are around for what you give them leave when it stops.

quotes.text: It matters not what one says, but what one feels; also, not how one feels on one particular day, but how one feels at all times.
quotes.plain: Happiness is your steady inner state, not a good day or what you tell people.

quotes.text: Folly is ever troubled with weariness of itself.
quotes.plain: A fool can't stand his own company and is always restless.

quotes.text: Do you not think, then, that some such wholesome advice as this could be given you: “Live among men as if God beheld you; speak with God as if men were listening”?
quotes.plain: Be the same person in public and in private.

quotes.text: We can get rid of most sins, if we have a witness who stands near us when we are likely to go wrong.
quotes.plain: Picture someone you respect watching you. You will do better.

quotes.text: Death, however, should be looked in the face by young and old alike. We are not summoned according to our rating on the censor’s list.
quotes.plain: Death doesn't go by age or rank. It can come for anyone, so don't act like you have unlimited time.

quotes.text: That man is happiest, and is secure in his own possession of himself, who can await the morrow without apprehension.
quotes.plain: If tomorrow doesn't scare you, you own yourself.

quotes.text: When a man has said: “I have lived!”, every morning he arises he receives a bonus.
quotes.plain: Close each day like it was complete, and every new morning is a gift.

quotes.text: There are more things, Lucilius, likely to frighten us than there are to crush us; we suffer more often in imagination than in reality.
quotes.plain: Fear shows up far more than real disaster does. Most of your suffering happens in your head.

quotes.text: We are in the habit of exaggerating, or imagining, or anticipating, sorrow.
quotes.plain: You blow problems up, invent them, or feel them ahead of time.

quotes.text: How often has the unexpected happened! How often has the expected never come to pass!
quotes.plain: Your predictions about the worst are wrong more often than you think.

quotes.text: You will suffer soon enough, when it arrives; so look forward meanwhile to better things.
quotes.plain: If the pain comes, you can feel it then. Don't pay for it twice.

quotes.text: We let ourselves drift with every breeze; we are frightened at uncertainties, just as if they were certain.
quotes.plain: You treat maybes like facts and get scared of them.

quotes.text: “The fool, with all his other faults, has this also, he is always getting ready to live.”
quotes.plain: Stop prepping to start. Start.

quotes.text: He will have many masters who makes his body his master, who is over-fearful in its behalf, who judges everything according to the body.
quotes.plain: Let comfort and fear of discomfort run you and you will answer to everyone.

quotes.text: Virtue is held too cheap by the man who counts his body too dear.
quotes.plain: If protecting your comfort matters most, you will never do anything hard or right.

quotes.text: If you are empty-handed, the highwayman passes you by; even along an infested road, the poor may travel in peace.
quotes.plain: Having little means little to lose and little to fear.

quotes.text: The beginning is in our own power; fortune decides the issue, but I do not allow her to pass sentence upon myself.
quotes.plain: You control the effort. Luck controls the result, and it doesn't get to decide your worth.

quotes.text: “He who needs riches least, enjoys riches most.”
quotes.plain: Needing less money makes you freer when you have it.

quotes.text: While he puzzles over increasing his wealth, he forgets how to use it.
quotes.plain: Chasing more money can make you forget to live on it.

quotes.text: “The fool’s life is empty of gratitude and full of fears; its course lies wholly toward the future.”
quotes.plain: Always chasing what is next, you never enjoy what you have and you stay scared.

quotes.text: Fix a limit which you will not even desire to pass, should you have the power.
quotes.plain: Decide ahead what is enough, and hold the line when you could have more.

quotes.text: As to what the future’s uncertain lot has in store, why should I demand of Fortune that she give, rather than demand of myself that I should not crave?
quotes.plain: Instead of begging luck for more, want less.

quotes.text: Philosophy is no trick to catch the public; it is not devised for show. It is a matter, not of words, but of facts.
quotes.plain: Ideas only count when you live them.

quotes.text: “If you live according to nature, you will never be poor; if you live according to opinion, you will never be rich.”
quotes.plain: What your body needs is cheap. What other people's opinions demand has no end.

quotes.text: Nature’s wants are slight; the demands of opinion are boundless.
quotes.plain: You need little. Keeping up appearances takes everything.

quotes.text: Hunger costs but little; squeamishness costs much.
quotes.plain: Basic needs are cheap. Being picky is what gets expensive.

quotes.text: Why of your own accord postpone your real life to the distant future?
quotes.plain: Don't wait for a bigger bank account to start living.

quotes.text: But in every age, what is enough remains the same.
quotes.plain: Enough doesn't grow with your income unless you let it.

quotes.text: “The acquisition of riches has been for many men, not an end, but a change, of troubles.”
quotes.plain: Getting rich doesn't end your problems. It swaps them for new ones.

quotes.text: It is precisely in times of immunity from care that the soul should toughen itself beforehand for occasions of greater stress, and it is while Fortune is kind that it should fortify itself against her violence.
quotes.plain: Get tough when life is easy, because that is when you can.

quotes.text: If you would not have a man flinch when the crisis comes, train him before it comes.
quotes.plain: Do the hard practice now so the real test doesn't break you.

quotes.text: Let us practise our strokes on the “dummy”; let us become intimate with poverty, so that Fortune may not catch us off our guard.
quotes.plain: Practice living on little so losing money can't wreck you.

quotes.text: Why wait until there is nothing left for you to crave? That time will never come.
quotes.plain: You will never feel done wanting. Pick your enough now.

quotes.text: Would you rather be poor and sated, or rich and hungry?
quotes.plain: Having enough beats having a lot and still wanting more.

quotes.text: Prosperity is not only greedy, but it also lies exposed to the greed of others.
quotes.plain: The more you have, the more you want, and the more others want from you.

quotes.text: But all that is added to your successes will be added to your fears.
quotes.plain: Every step up gives you more to lose.

quotes.text: A trifling debt makes a man your debtor; a large one makes him an enemy.
quotes.plain: Small favors build loyalty. Huge ones breed resentment.

quotes.text: Prove your words by your deeds.
quotes.plain: Talk is cheap. Show it.

quotes.text: It is indeed a hard undertaking, and I do not say that the philosopher can always keep the same pace. But he can always travel the same path.
quotes.plain: You won't always move fast, but you can always head the right way.

quotes.text: Poverty will keep for you your true and tried friends; you will be rid of the men who were not seeking you for yourself, but for something which you have.
quotes.plain: Having nothing shows you who actually likes you.

quotes.text: O when will that time come, when no one shall tell lies to compliment you!
quotes.plain: Flattery is everywhere. Real honesty is rare and worth finding.

quotes.text: It means much not to be spoiled by intimacy with riches; and he is truly great who is poor amidst riches.
quotes.plain: Real strength is having plenty and not needing it.

quotes.text: No man is born rich. Every man, when he first sees light, is commanded to be content with milk and rags. Such is our beginning, and yet kingdoms are all too small for us!
quotes.plain: Everybody starts with nothing, yet nothing is ever enough.

quotes.text: Your greatest difficulty is with yourself; for you are your own stumbling-block.
quotes.plain: The main obstacle is you.

quotes.text: You do not know what you want. You are better at approving the right course than at following it out. You see where the true happiness lies, but you have not the courage to attain it.
quotes.plain: You know what's right and can't make yourself do it. Courage, not knowledge, is missing.

quotes.text: The deep flood of time will roll over us; some few great men will raise their heads above it, and, though destined at the last to depart into the same realms of silence, will battle against oblivion and maintain their ground for long.
quotes.plain: Time erases almost everyone. The ones who last do it by fighting the current.

quotes.text: “If you wish,” said he, “to make Pythocles rich, do not add to his store of money, but subtract from his desires.”
quotes.plain: Want less and you are richer, faster than earning more.

quotes.text: But no one is compelled to pursue prosperity at top speed; it means something to call a halt, even if one does not offer resistance, instead of pressing eagerly after favouring fortune.
quotes.plain: Nobody makes you chase more. Stopping is a choice you can make.

quotes.text: It is so, my dear Lucilius; there are a few men whom slavery holds fast, but there are many more who hold fast to slavery.
quotes.plain: Plenty of people complain about their trap and refuse to leave it.

quotes.text: No man can swim ashore and take his baggage with him.
quotes.plain: Escape means leaving things behind. Stop trying to keep everything.

quotes.text: Take anyone off his guard, young, old, or middle-aged; you will find that all are equally afraid of death, and equally ignorant of life.
quotes.plain: People fear dying and haven't figured out how to live.

quotes.text: No one has anything finished, because we have kept putting off into the future all our undertakings.
quotes.plain: Nothing gets done when it's always for later.

quotes.text: Men do not care how nobly they live, but only how long, although it is within the reach of every man to live nobly, but within no man’s power to live long.
quotes.plain: You can't control how long you live. You can control how well.

quotes.text: Do you ask what is the foundation of a sound mind? It is, not to find joy in useless things.
quotes.plain: A steady mind starts with not getting your happiness from junk.

quotes.text: Above all, my dear Lucilius, make this your business: learn how to feel joy.
quotes.plain: Joy is a skill. Practice it on purpose.

quotes.text: Real joy, believe me, is a stern matter.
quotes.plain: Deep satisfaction comes from hard, serious things, not from fun.

quotes.text: There are only a few who control themselves and their affairs by a guiding purpose; the rest do not proceed; they are merely swept along, like objects afloat in a river.
quotes.plain: Most people drift. Having a purpose is rare and it sets you apart.

quotes.text: We must make it our aim already to have lived long enough.
quotes.plain: Live so that if it ended today, you would not feel cheated.

quotes.text: And if this seems surprising to you, I shall add that which will surprise you still more: Some men have left off living before they have begun.
quotes.plain: Plenty of people are done with life before they ever really started.

quotes.text: Why, indeed, is it necessary to summon trouble, which must be endured soon enough when it has once arrived, or to anticipate trouble and ruin the present through fear of the future?
quotes.plain: Worrying early just wrecks today and fixes nothing.

quotes.text: It is indeed foolish to be unhappy now because you may be unhappy at some future time.
quotes.plain: Don't suffer today over something that might happen later.

quotes.text: You will thus understand that what you fear is either insignificant or short-lived.
quotes.plain: Look straight at the worst case and it shrinks.

quotes.text: Remember, however, before all else, to strip things of all that disturbs and confuses, and to see what each is at bottom; you will then comprehend that they contain nothing fearful except the actual fear.
quotes.plain: Strip away the drama and most scary things are just scary because you're afraid.

quotes.text: We should strip the mask, not only from men, but from things, and restore to each object its own aspect.
quotes.plain: See things as they actually are, without the costume fear puts on them.

quotes.text: Slight thou art, if I can bear thee; short thou art if I cannot bear thee!
quotes.plain: Pain is either small enough to bear or short enough to end.

quotes.text: You were born to these perils. Let us think of everything that can happen as something which will happen.
quotes.plain: Expect the hard stuff in advance and it can't ambush you.

quotes.text: Counting even yesterday, all past time is lost time; the very day which we are now spending is shared between ourselves and death.
quotes.plain: Yesterday is gone and today is already being used up.

quotes.text: It is not the last drop that empties the water-clock, but all that which previously has flowed out; similarly, the final hour when we cease to exist does not of itself bring death; it merely of itself completes the death-process.
quotes.plain: You have been dying one day at a time. The last hour just finishes it.

quotes.text: The things which we actually need are free for all, or else cheap; nature craves only bread and water.
quotes.plain: What you actually need costs almost nothing.

quotes.text: Meantime, you are engaged in making of yourself the sort of person in whose company you would not dare to sin.
quotes.plain: Become someone you would be ashamed to let down.

quotes.text: “The time when you should most of all withdraw into yourself is when you are forced to be in a crowd.”
quotes.plain: When the room is loud, go inward and keep your own head.

quotes.text: Alone, you are too close to a rascal.
quotes.plain: Alone with your worst impulses, you can talk yourself into anything.

quotes.text: Even the most timid man can deliver a bold speech.
quotes.plain: Talking tough is easy. What you do under pressure is the real test.

quotes.text: There is no fixed count of our years. You do not know where death awaits you; so be ready for it everywhere.
quotes.plain: Nobody knows their number. Live like you are ready.

quotes.text: He who has learned to die has unlearned slavery; he is above any external power, or, at any rate, he is beyond it.
quotes.plain: Once you stop fearing the worst, nobody can hold anything over you.

quotes.text: There is only one chain which binds us to life, and that is the love of life.
quotes.plain: Clinging to life is what makes everything else feel like a threat.

quotes.text: Count your years, and you will be ashamed to desire and pursue the same things you desired in your boyhood days.
quotes.plain: Grow up. You've been chasing the same cheap wants for years.

quotes.text: Of this one thing make sure against your dying day, let your faults die before you die.
quotes.plain: Kill your bad habits while you still can.

quotes.text: Just as crimes, even if they have not been detected when they were committed, do not allow anxiety to end with them; so with guilty pleasures, regret remains even after the pleasures are over.
quotes.plain: The thrill passes in minutes. The regret sticks around.

quotes.text: This matter cannot be delegated to someone else.
quotes.plain: Nobody can do the inner work for you.

quotes.text: No man is able to borrow or buy a sound mind; in fact, as it seems to me, even though sound minds were for sale, they would not find buyers. Depraved minds, however, are bought and sold every day.
quotes.plain: You can't buy a clear head, and nobody even wants to. Corruption always finds a market.

quotes.text: You need a change of soul rather than a change of climate.
quotes.plain: Moving somewhere new won't fix what's wrong inside you.

quotes.text: “Why do you wonder that globe-trotting does not help you, seeing that you always take yourself with you? The reason which set you wandering is ever at your heels.”
quotes.plain: You can't run from yourself. The problem travels with you.

quotes.text: The person you are matters more than the place to which you go; for that reason we should not make the mind a bondsman to any one place.
quotes.plain: Who you are matters more than where you are.

quotes.text: At times be harsh with yourself.
quotes.plain: Hold yourself accountable. Nobody else will do it as well.

quotes.text: Do not count the number of those who inspire fear in you.
quotes.plain: Stop tallying what threatens you. It's never as many as it feels like.

quotes.text: Nature has so ordered it that, as only one has given you life, so only one will take it away.
quotes.plain: Plenty of people threaten you, but only one thing can actually end you.

quotes.text: I have never wished to cater to the crowd; for what I know, they do not approve, and what they approve, I do not know.
quotes.plain: Real knowledge and popular taste rarely overlap. Pick knowledge.

quotes.text: The favour of ignoble men can be won only by ignoble means.
quotes.plain: Chasing the crowd's approval means becoming small to get it.

quotes.text: He who does not wish to die cannot have wished to live.
quotes.plain: Life came with the ending built in. You can't take one without the other.

quotes.text: But who is not near death? It is ready for us in all places and at all times.
quotes.plain: Nobody is far from death, so stop acting like you have forever.

quotes.text: We do not fear death; we fear the thought of death.
quotes.plain: The dread lives in your head. Death itself is always the same distance away.

quotes.text: Do you, however, always think on death in order that you may never fear it.
quotes.plain: Look at death often enough and it stops scaring you.

quotes.text: Be deaf to those who love you most of all; they pray for bad things with good intentions.
quotes.plain: People who love you can want the wrong things for you. Don't take all their advice.

quotes.text: By so much you are better! Rise, draw a fresh breath, and surmount that hill, if possible, at a single spurt!
quotes.plain: The harder you push up the hill, the better you get. Catch your breath and go again.

quotes.text: Work is the sustenance of noble minds.
quotes.plain: Serious people are fed by hard work, not by rest.

quotes.text: I forbid you to be cast down or depressed. It is not enough if you do not shrink from work; ask for it.
quotes.plain: Don't just put up with the work. Go looking for it.

quotes.text: One may leap to heaven from the very slums.
quotes.plain: Where you start doesn't cap where you can get to.

quotes.text: Live just as if I were sure to get news of your doings, nay, as if I were sure to behold them.
quotes.plain: Act like someone you respect is watching everything you do.

quotes.text: We break up life into little bits, and fritter it away.
quotes.plain: Constant restarts chop your one life into scraps.

quotes.text: Would you know what makes men greedy for the future? It is because no one has yet found himself.
quotes.plain: People who don't know who they are keep chasing the next thing.

quotes.text: Take command, and utter some word which posterity will remember.
quotes.plain: Stop echoing others. Say something of your own worth remembering.

quotes.text: Remembering is merely safeguarding something entrusted to the memory; knowing, however, means making everything your own; it means not depending upon the copy and not all the time glancing back at the master.
quotes.plain: Quoting wise people isn't wisdom. It's yours once you can act without checking the source.

quotes.text: Let there be a difference between yourself and your book! How long shall you be a learner? From now on be a teacher as well!
quotes.plain: At some point you have to stop only studying and start producing.

quotes.text: Men who have made these discoveries before us are not our masters, but our guides.
quotes.plain: Learn from the greats, but you're allowed to go further than them.

quotes.text: If a man’s acts are out of harmony, his soul is crooked.
quotes.plain: When what you do and what you say don't match, something in you is off.

quotes.text: A shifting of the will indicates that the mind is at sea, heading in various directions, according to the course of the wind.
quotes.plain: If your wants change every day, you're drifting, not steering.

quotes.text: Fortune has no jurisdiction over character.
quotes.plain: Luck can take your stuff. It can't touch who you are.

quotes.text: In death there is nothing harmful; for there must exist something to which it is harmful.
quotes.plain: Death can't hurt you because there's no you left for it to hurt.

quotes.text: You must die erect and unyielding.
quotes.plain: Don't beg or cave when the hard thing comes.

quotes.text: You cannot escape necessities, but you can overcome them.
quotes.plain: You can't dodge the hard parts of life, but you can beat them.

quotes.text: Proceed with steady step, and if you would have all things under your control, put yourself under the control of reason; if reason becomes your ruler, you will become ruler over many.
quotes.plain: Rule yourself with clear thinking first and everything else gets easier to rule.

quotes.text: You can show me no man who knows how he began to crave that which he craves.
quotes.plain: Most of our wants came from nowhere we chose. Question them.

quotes.text: Utility measures our needs; but by what standard can you check the superfluous?
quotes.plain: Needs have a limit. Wants don't, so you have to set the limit yourself.

quotes.text: Then it is that the height of unhappiness is reached, when men are not only attracted, but even pleased, by shameful things, and when there is no longer any room for a cure, now that those things which once were vices have become habits.
quotes.plain: The worst point is when your bad habit feels fine to you and you've stopped wanting out.

quotes.text: My terrors should be quieted, my irritations soothed, my illusions shaken off, my indulgences checked, my greed rebuked.
quotes.plain: The real job is inside: calm the fear, the irritation, the illusions, the cravings.

quotes.text: No man ought to glory except in that which is his own.
quotes.plain: Only take pride in what can't be handed to someone else.

quotes.text: Praise the quality in him which cannot be given or snatched away, that which is the peculiar property of the man.
quotes.plain: Judge people, and yourself, by what can't be bought or taken.

quotes.text: Very often the things that cost nothing cost us the most heavily; I can show you many objects the quest and acquisition of which have wrested freedom from our hands.
quotes.plain: The stuff you chase for free often costs you your freedom.

quotes.text: We should belong to ourselves, if only these things did not belong to us.
quotes.plain: Your possessions and ambitions own you more than you own them.

quotes.text: He that owns himself has lost nothing. But how few men are blessed with ownership of self!
quotes.plain: If you hold yourself together, nothing outside can really take anything from you.

quotes.text: If your deeds are honourable, let everybody know them; if base, what matters it that no one knows them, as long as you yourself know them?
quotes.plain: Nobody seeing it doesn't make it clean. You know.

quotes.text: Philosophy did not find Plato already a nobleman; it made him one.
quotes.plain: Nobody starts great. You become it.

quotes.text: This is what happens when you hurry through a maze; the faster you go, the worse you are entangled.
quotes.plain: Rushing blindly through confusion makes the mess worse.

quotes.text: He who would arrive at the appointed end must follow a single road and not wander through many ways.
quotes.plain: Pick one road and stay on it.

quotes.text: Show me a man who is not a slave; one is a slave to lust, another to greed, another to ambition, and all men are slaves to fear.
quotes.plain: Everybody is ruled by something. Know which master is yours.

quotes.text: No servitude is more disgraceful than that which is self-imposed.
quotes.plain: The chains you put on yourself are the worst ones.

quotes.text: That which annoys us does not necessarily injure us; but we are driven into wild rage by our luxurious lives, so that whatever does not answer our whims arouses our anger.
quotes.plain: Most of what makes you furious is only annoying. Comfort made you sensitive.

quotes.text: And no one can live happily who has regard to himself alone and transforms everything into a question of his own utility; you must live for your neighbour, if you would live for yourself.
quotes.plain: A life that's only about you is a small, unhappy one.

quotes.text: Infinitely swift is the flight of time, as those see more clearly who are looking backwards.
quotes.plain: Time looks slow while you're in it and fast once it's gone.

quotes.text: Show me that the good in life does not depend upon life’s length, but upon the use we make of it; also, that it is possible, or rather usual, for a man who has lived long to have lived too little.
quotes.plain: A long life isn't a full one. What you did with it is.

quotes.text: Say to me when I lie down to sleep: “You may not wake again!” And when I have waked: “You may not go to sleep again!”
quotes.plain: Treat every day like it could be the last one and the first one.

quotes.text: The evil that afflicts us is not external, it is within us, situated in our very vitals; for that reason we attain soundness with all the more difficulty, because we do not know that we are diseased.
quotes.plain: The problem is inside, and it's hard to fix because we don't see it.

quotes.text: There is nothing that will not surrender to persistent treatment, to concentrated and careful attention; however much the timber may be bent, you can make it straight again.
quotes.plain: Steady, focused effort straightens anything, even a warped habit.

quotes.text: Learning virtue means unlearning vice.
quotes.plain: Getting better means dropping the bad stuff you picked up.

quotes.text: The mind must, therefore, be forced to make a beginning; from then on, the medicine is not bitter; for just as soon as it is curing us it begins to give pleasure.
quotes.plain: Starting is the hard part. Once it's working, it feels good.

quotes.text: Perspiration should flow only after toil.
quotes.plain: Earn the easy stuff first.

quotes.text: And what is freedom, you ask? It means not being a slave to any circumstance, to any constraint, to any chance; it means compelling Fortune to enter the lists on equal terms.
quotes.plain: Freedom is not letting circumstances run you.

quotes.text: If any vice rend your heart, cast it away from you; and if you cannot be rid of it in any other way, pluck out your heart also.
quotes.plain: Whatever habit is tearing you apart, get rid of it, whatever it takes.

quotes.text: I should accordingly deem more fortunate the man who has never had any trouble with himself; but the other, I feel, has deserved better of himself, who has won a victory over the meanness of his own nature, and has not gently led himself, but has wrestled his way, to wisdom.
quotes.plain: Having it easy is lucky. Fighting your own nature and winning earns more respect.

quotes.text: Choose as a guide one whom you will admire more when you see him act than when you hear him speak.
quotes.plain: Follow people whose actions beat their words.

quotes.text: Why will no man confess his faults? Because he is still in their grasp; only he who is awake can recount his dream, and similarly a confession of sin is a proof of sound mind.
quotes.plain: Being able to admit your faults means you've started to wake up from them.

quotes.text: Do not study philosophy merely during your spare time.
quotes.plain: Don't give what matters only your leftover hours.

quotes.text: Death is non-existence, and I know already what that means. What was before me will happen again after me.
quotes.plain: You've already been dead once, before birth, and it didn't hurt.

quotes.text: We mortals also are lighted and extinguished; the period of suffering comes in between, but on either side there is a deep peace.
quotes.plain: Pain only exists in the middle. Before and after is peace.

quotes.text: I shall never be frightened when the last hour comes; I am already prepared and do not plan a whole day ahead.
quotes.plain: Live ready, with nothing left on hold.

quotes.text: The place where one lives, however, can contribute little towards tranquillity; it is the mind which must make everything agreeable to itself.
quotes.plain: Peace comes from your head, not your location.

quotes.text: You need not suppose that the soul is at peace when the body is still. Sometimes quiet means disquiet.
quotes.plain: Resting isn't the same as being at peace.

quotes.text: The much occupied man has no time for wantonness, and it is an obvious commonplace that the evils of leisure can be shaken off by hard work.
quotes.plain: Stay busy with real work and the temptations lose their grip.

quotes.text: So with greed, ambition, and the other evils of the mind, you may be sure that they do most harm when they are hidden behind a pretence of soundness.
quotes.plain: The worst vices are the ones that look respectable.

quotes.text: You may therefore be sure that you are at peace with yourself, when no noise reaches you, when no word shakes you out of yourself, whether it be of flattery or of threat, or merely an empty sound buzzing about you with unmeaning din.
quotes.plain: You're steady when neither praise nor threats can move you.

quotes.text: None of us is the same man in old age that he was in youth; nor the same on the morrow as on the day preceding.
quotes.plain: You're changing constantly, so don't cling to who you were.

quotes.text: We go down twice into the same river, and yet into a different river.
quotes.plain: Nothing stays put, including you.

quotes.text: Will you not stop fearing lest that may happen once which really happens every day?
quotes.plain: You die a little each day already. One more time is nothing new.

quotes.text: There is a pleasure in being in one’s own company as long as possible, when a man has made himself worth enjoying.
quotes.plain: Become someone you like being alone with.

quotes.text: No, it is a characteristic of real joy that it never ceases, and never changes into its opposite.
quotes.plain: Real joy doesn't fade or flip into its opposite. If it can, it was only pleasure.

quotes.text: Folly is pursued, and confronted, by peril. It blenches at everything; it is unprepared; it is frightened even by auxiliary troops.
quotes.plain: A fool is scared of everything, even his own side. Fear lives in unprepared minds.

quotes.text: None of us goes deep below the surface. We skim the top only, and we regard the smattering of time spent in the search for wisdom as enough and to spare for a busy man.
quotes.plain: We give wisdom the scraps of our time and call it enough.

quotes.text: What hinders us most of all is that we are too readily satisfied with ourselves; if we meet with someone who calls us good men, or sensible men, or holy men, we see ourselves in his description.
quotes.plain: Flattery is easy to believe. We start seeing ourselves as the kind words say we are.

quotes.text: “All men swear that I am the son of Jupiter, but this wound cries out that I am mortal.”
quotes.plain: Everyone can call you a god, and one wound still reminds you that you're human.

quotes.text: Joy is the goal which you desire to reach, but you are wandering from the path, if you expect to reach your goal while you are in the midst of riches and official titles, in other words, if you seek joy in the midst of cares.
quotes.plain: You can't reach peace by piling on titles and money. That road runs through more worry.

quotes.text: How small is the amount which will satisfy nature? A very little will send her away contented.
quotes.plain: What your body needs is tiny. The rest is appetite.

quotes.text: It is not the natural hunger of our bellies that costs us dear, but our solicitous cravings.
quotes.plain: Need is cheap. Craving is what costs you.

quotes.text: He really lives who is made use of by many; he really lives who makes use of himself.
quotes.plain: Living means being useful to others and to yourself.

quotes.text: Those men, however, who creep into a hole and grow torpid are no better off in their homes than if they were in their tombs. Right there on the marble lintel of the house of such a man you may inscribe his name, for he has died before he is dead.
quotes.plain: Hiding in a hole and going numb is dying early.

quotes.text: Let us cease to desire that which we have been desiring.
quotes.plain: Stop wanting the same things you've always wanted. They haven't worked.

quotes.text: I am endeavouring to live every day as if it were a complete life.
quotes.plain: Treat each day as a whole life, not a rehearsal.

quotes.text: I do not indeed snatch it up as if it were my last; I do regard it, however, as if it might even be my last.
quotes.plain: Don't rush through today. Just don't assume there's another.

quotes.text: The man who does something under orders is not unhappy; he is unhappy who does something against his will.
quotes.plain: The misery is in doing it unwillingly. Choose the work and it stops being a chain.

quotes.text: We must make ready for death before we make ready for life.
quotes.plain: Face your end first and you'll live without flinching.

quotes.text: Life is well enough furnished, but we are too greedy with regard to its furnishings; something always seems to us lacking, and will always seem lacking.
quotes.plain: There's enough. The feeling that something's missing never ends.

quotes.text: To have lived long enough depends neither upon our years nor upon our days, but upon our minds.
quotes.plain: A full life is about how you think, not how long you last.

quotes.text: We are deceived by those who would have us believe that a multitude of affairs blocks their pursuit of liberal studies; they make a pretence of their engagements, and multiply them, when their engagements are merely with themselves.
quotes.plain: Being too busy is mostly an excuse we build ourselves.

quotes.text: It is in the power of any man to despise all things, but of no man to possess all things. The shortest cut to riches is to despise riches.
quotes.plain: You can't own everything, but you can need nothing. That's the fastest way to rich.

quotes.text: Let not the eyes be dry when we have lost a friend, nor let them overflow. We may weep, but we must not wail.
quotes.plain: Grieve, but don't make a show of it or drown in it.

quotes.text: To me, the thought of my dead friends is sweet and appealing. For I have had them as if I should one day lose them; I have lost them as if I have them still.
quotes.plain: Love people as if you'll lose them, and you'll keep them after.

quotes.text: Let us greedily enjoy our friends, because we do not know how long this privilege will be ours.
quotes.plain: Spend time with your people now. You don't know how long you get.

quotes.text: You have buried one whom you loved; look about for someone to love. It is better to replace your friend than to weep for him.
quotes.plain: Don't mourn alone forever. Go love someone.

quotes.text: I should prefer you to abandon grief, rather than have grief abandon you; and you should stop grieving as soon as possible, since, even if you wish to do so, it is impossible to keep it up for a long time.
quotes.plain: Put grief down on purpose before it just wears out.

quotes.text: Nothing becomes offensive so quickly as grief; when fresh, it finds someone to console it and attracts one or another to itself; but after becoming chronic, it is ridiculed, and rightly.
quotes.plain: Grief that's held onto too long turns stale, even to you.

quotes.text: Now is the time for you to reflect, not only that all things are mortal, but also that their mortality is subject to no fixed law. Whatever can happen at any time can happen to-day.
quotes.plain: Anything that could happen someday could happen today. Plan like it.

quotes.text: I want to challenge every hazard; I want to cry: “Why keep me waiting, Fortune? Enter the lists! Behold, I am ready for you!”
quotes.plain: Call fate out. Be ready for whatever comes.

quotes.text: I want something to overcome, something on which I may test my endurance.
quotes.plain: Give me a hard thing to push against. That's how you find your limit.

quotes.text: The cures for the spirit also have been discovered by the ancients; but it is our task to learn the method and the time of treatment.
quotes.plain: The advice already exists. The work is applying the right piece at the right time.

quotes.text: Never shall this flesh drive me to feel fear, or to assume any pretence that is unworthy of a good man.
quotes.plain: Don't let your body's comfort make you fake it or fold.

quotes.text: Let us be brave in the face of hazards. Let us not fear wrongs, or wounds, or bonds, or poverty.
quotes.plain: Don't fear what can be done to you. Wounds, chains, and poverty are survivable.

quotes.text: It is either the end, or a process of change. I have no fear of ceasing to exist; it is the same as not having begun.
quotes.plain: Death is either nothing or a change. Not being is just like before you were born.

quotes.text: A great man can spring from a hovel; so can a beautiful and great soul from an ugly and insignificant body.
quotes.plain: Greatness doesn't care where you start or what you look like.

quotes.text: That which is not free cannot be honourable; for fear means slavery.
quotes.plain: Fear makes you a slave. Nothing done out of fear is worth admiring.

quotes.text: I should prefer to be free from torture; but if the time comes when it must be endured, I shall desire that I may conduct myself therein with bravery, honour, and courage.
quotes.plain: Nobody asks for hardship, but if it comes, ask to face it well.

quotes.text: The conclusion is, not that hardships are desirable, but that virtue is desirable, which enables us patiently to endure hardships.
quotes.plain: Don't chase pain. Build the strength to take it.

quotes.text: Clothe yourself with a hero’s courage, and withdraw for a little space from the opinions of the common man. Form a proper conception of the image of virtue, a thing of exceeding beauty and grandeur; this image is not to be worshipped by us with incense or garlands, but with sweat and blood.
quotes.plain: Ignore the crowd for a while. Greatness is paid for in sweat, not applause.

quotes.text: If you have nothing to stir you up and rouse you to action, nothing which will test your resolution by its threats and hostilities; if you recline in unshaken comfort, it is not tranquillity; it is merely a flat calm.
quotes.plain: Comfort without challenge isn't peace. It's stagnation.

quotes.text: “I should prefer that Fortune keep me in her camp rather than in the lap of luxury. If I am tortured, but bear it bravely, all is well; if I die, but die bravely, it is also well.”
quotes.plain: Better to be tested by fate than spoiled by comfort. Bear it bravely and it's fine either way.

quotes.text: To boast of our retirement is but idle self-seeking.
quotes.plain: Announcing your retreat from the world is just another way to be noticed.

quotes.text: When you withdraw from the world your business is to talk with yourself, not to have men talk about you.
quotes.plain: Alone time is for talking to yourself honestly, not for being talked about.

quotes.text: Do just what people are fond of doing when they talk about their neighbours, speak ill of yourself when by yourself; then you will become accustomed both to speak and to hear the truth.
quotes.plain: Criticize yourself in private the way people criticize others. You'll get used to the truth.

quotes.text: You are mistaken if you think that you will get any assistance from this quarter; it is not a physician that dwells here, but a sick man.
quotes.plain: I'm not a cure, I'm a patient working on it too. Don't put me on a pedestal.

quotes.text: Would that in earlier days you had been minded to follow this purpose! Would that we were not discussing the happy life in plain view of death!
quotes.plain: It's a shame to start living wisely only when death is in sight. Start now.

quotes.text: Let us do what men are wont to do when they are late in setting forth, and wish to make up for lost time by increasing their speed, let us ply the spur.
quotes.plain: Started late? Go faster, not slower.

quotes.text: To be able to hold your spirit in check, you must first stop the runaway flight of the body.
quotes.plain: To calm your mind, stop running around.

quotes.text: Give your eyes time to unlearn what they have seen, and your ears to grow accustomed to more wholesome words.
quotes.plain: Change what you look at and listen to, and your cravings change.

quotes.text: There is no evil that does not offer inducements.
quotes.plain: Every vice comes with a reward. That's why it works on you.

quotes.text: Vices tempt you by the rewards which they offer; but in the life of which I speak, you must live without being paid.
quotes.plain: Vices pay you right now. Discipline asks you to work for nothing up front.

quotes.text: Scarcely will a whole life-time suffice to bring our vices into subjection and to make them accept the yoke, swollen as they are by long-continued indulgence; and still less, if we cut into our brief span by any interruptions.
quotes.plain: Beating bad habits takes a lifetime of steady work. Every break makes it longer.

quotes.text: Humanity is well situated, because no man is unhappy except by his own fault.
quotes.plain: Nobody is truly unhappy unless they let themselves be.

quotes.text: Would you be free from the restraint of your body? Live in it as if you were about to leave it.
quotes.plain: Live loose. Hold nothing, including your body, like it's permanent.

quotes.text: Our souls have been made ready to meet poverty; but our riches have held out. We have armed ourselves to scorn pain; but we have had the good fortune to possess sound and healthy bodies, and so have never been forced to put this virtue to the test.
quotes.plain: Comfort hides how untested you are. Your strength hasn't been tried yet.

quotes.text: The reason we make mistakes is because we all consider the parts of life, but never life as a whole.
quotes.plain: We fuss over pieces of life and forget to ask what the whole thing is for.

quotes.text: Our plans miscarry because they have no aim.
quotes.plain: Plans fail because there's no target.

quotes.text: When a man does not know what harbour he is making for, no wind is the right wind.
quotes.plain: If you don't know where you're going, no luck will help.

quotes.text: Allow any man who so desires to insult you and work you wrong; but if only virtue dwells with you, you will suffer nothing.
quotes.plain: Insults only hurt if you give up your own character.

quotes.text: There is nothing that does not have its old age; the intervals are merely unequal at which Nature sends forth all these things towards the same goal.
quotes.plain: Everything ages and ends. Nothing is special enough to be exempt.

quotes.text: To a luxurious man, a simple life is a penalty; to a lazy man, work is punishment; the dandy pities the diligent man; to the slothful, studies are torture.
quotes.plain: Hard is relative. What feels like punishment is just what you're soft about.

quotes.text: These actions are not essentially difficult; it is we ourselves that are soft and flabby.
quotes.plain: The thing isn't hard. We've gone soft.

quotes.text: It matters not only what you see, but with what eyes you see it; our souls are too dull of vision to perceive the truth.
quotes.plain: How you see matters more than what you see.

quotes.text: It is not a cause for wonder that one is not tossed about when the weather is calm; reserve your wonderment for cases where a man is lifted up when all others sink, and keeps his footing when all others are prostrate.
quotes.plain: Calm in calm weather proves nothing. Respect the one standing when everyone else is down.

quotes.text: What element of evil is there in torture and in the other things which we call hardships? It seems to me that there is this evil, that the mind sags, and bends, and collapses.
quotes.plain: Hardship's real damage is when your mind gives out.

quotes.text: There remains much more of the road than we have put behind us; but the greater part of progress is the desire to progress.
quotes.plain: Most of the road is still ahead, and wanting to move is half of moving.

quotes.text: Let us see to it that all time belongs to us. This, however, cannot be unless first of all our own selves begin to belong to us.
quotes.plain: To own your time, you first have to own yourself.

quotes.text: Neither the Persians, nor the far-off Medes, nor any warlike race that lies beyond the Dahae; not these, but greed, ambition, and the fear of death that has conquered the conquerors of the world.
quotes.plain: The real enemies to conquer are greed, ambition, and fear of death.

quotes.text: Then, too, we keep adjourning our own cases, saying: “As soon as I am done with this, I shall settle down to hard work,” or: “If I ever set this troublesome matter in order, I shall devote myself to study.”
quotes.plain: "After this one thing, I'll start" never ends. There's always another thing.

quotes.text: Now all that which the crowd gapes after, ebbs and flows. Fortune gives us nothing which we can really own.
quotes.plain: What the crowd chases rises and falls. Fortune never actually gives you anything to keep.

quotes.text: That is the trouble with every sort of ambition; it does not look back. Nor is it ambition alone that is fickle, but also every sort of craving, because it always begins where it ought to end.
quotes.plain: Ambition never looks back at how far you've come. Craving starts where it should stop.

quotes.text: The gods are not disdainful or envious; they open the door to you; they lend a hand as you climb.
quotes.plain: The way up is open. Nothing's blocking you but you.

quotes.text: Like birds, who cower even at the whirr of an empty sling, we are distracted by mere sounds as well as by blows.
quotes.plain: We flinch at noise as much as at actual hits.

quotes.text: Whoever has largely surrendered himself to the power of Fortune has made for himself a huge web of disquietude, from which he cannot get free; if one would win a way to safety, there is but one road, to despise externals and to be contented with that which is honourable.
quotes.plain: Handing your peace to fortune builds a trap. The only way out is needing less from outside.

quotes.text: The most sensible man, therefore, as soon as he sees the dole being brought in, runs from the theatre; for he knows that one pays a high price for small favours. No one will grapple with him on the way out, or strike him as he departs; the quarrelling takes place where the prizes are.
quotes.plain: The smart one leaves the scramble. The fighting is always where the prizes are.

quotes.text: Do you ask why virtue needs nothing? Because it is pleased with what it has, and does not lust after that which it has not. Whatever is enough is abundant in the eyes of virtue.
quotes.plain: Being content with what you have makes you complete.

quotes.text: Let everything of this nature be added to us, and not stick fast to us, so that, if it is withdrawn, it may come away without tearing off any part of us.
quotes.plain: Own things so loosely that losing them costs you nothing of yourself.

quotes.text: Let us use these things, but not boast of them, and let us use them sparingly, as if they were given for safe-keeping and will be withdrawn.
quotes.plain: Use what you have lightly. It's on loan.

quotes.text: Few men have been permitted to lay aside prosperity gently. The rest all fall, together with the things amid which they have come into eminence, and they are weighted down by the very things which had before exalted them.
quotes.plain: Few people leave success gracefully. The rest get crushed by what raised them.

quotes.text: We should fortify ourselves against such calamities. But no wall can be erected against Fortune which she cannot take by storm; let us strengthen our inner defences. If the inner part be safe, man can be attacked, but never captured.
quotes.plain: Fortune can breach any wall. Make the inside strong and you can be hit but not taken.

quotes.text: Love reason! The love of reason will arm you against the greatest hardships.
quotes.plain: A clear mind is your best armor.

quotes.text: Past and future are both absent; we feel neither of them. But there can be no pain except as the result of what you feel.
quotes.plain: Past and future aren't here. You only hurt from what you feel now.

quotes.text: Let this be the kernel of my idea: let us say what we feel, and feel what we say; let speech harmonize with life.
quotes.plain: Say what you feel. Live what you say.

quotes.text: That man has fulfilled his promise who is the same person both when you see him and when you hear him.
quotes.plain: Be the same person in private and in public.

quotes.text: Our words should aim not to please, but to help.
quotes.plain: Don't try to impress. Try to help.

quotes.text: Why do you tickle my ears? Why do you entertain me? There is other business at hand; I am to be cauterized, operated upon, or put on a diet.
quotes.plain: I don't need to be entertained. I need the hard treatment.

quotes.text: When shall you learn all that there is to learn? When shall you so plant in your mind that which you have learned, that it cannot escape? When shall you put it all into practice?
quotes.plain: When do you stop learning and start doing?

quotes.text: He is not happy who only knows them, but he who does them.
quotes.plain: Knowing isn't enough. Do it.

quotes.text: We hasten towards virtue while hampered by vices. I am ashamed to say it; but we worship that which is honourable only in so far as we have time to spare.
quotes.plain: We chase the good life with bad habits dragging us, and only give it spare time.

quotes.text: Undisturbed by fears, unspoiled by pleasures, we shall be afraid neither of death nor of the gods; we shall know that death is no evil and that the gods are not powers of evil.
quotes.plain: Without fear or cheap pleasures, death and the gods stop being threats.

quotes.text: And it is a priceless good to be master of oneself.
quotes.plain: Mastering yourself is the best thing you can own.

quotes.text: Now what is more foolish than refusing to learn, simply because one has not been learning for a long time?
quotes.plain: Not having learned in the past is no reason to stay ignorant now.

quotes.text: Wisdom comes haphazard to no man.
quotes.plain: Nobody drifts into wisdom. You go get it.

quotes.text: Money will come of its own accord; titles will be given to you; influence and authority will perhaps be thrust upon you; but virtue will not fall upon you by chance.
quotes.plain: Money, titles and influence can land on you by luck. Character never does.

quotes.text: A dwarf is not tall, though he stand upon a mountain-top; a colossal statue will still be tall, though you place it in a well.
quotes.plain: Status does not make a man big and lowliness does not make him small.

quotes.text: If an evil has been pondered beforehand, the blow is gentle when it comes.
quotes.plain: Think through the bad outcome ahead of time and it hits softer.

quotes.text: To the fool, however, and to him who trusts in fortune, each event as it arrives “comes in a new and sudden form,” and a large part of evil, to the inexperienced, consists in its novelty.
quotes.plain: Much of what hurts is that it is new. Expect trouble and half the sting is gone.

quotes.text: We sometimes hear the inexperienced say: “I knew that this was in store for me.” But the wise man knows that all things are in store for him. Whatever happens, he says: “I knew it.”
quotes.plain: The wise man is never surprised, because he already counted on everything.

quotes.text: At whatever point you leave off living, provided you leave off nobly, your life is a whole.
quotes.plain: A life is complete if it is lived honorably, however long it runs.

quotes.text: It is not an important matter to live; all your slaves live, and so do all animals; but it is important to die honourably, sensibly, bravely.
quotes.plain: Staying alive is nothing special. Doing it, and dying, with courage is.

quotes.text: Reflect how long you have been doing the same thing: food, sleep, lust, this is one’s daily round.
quotes.plain: Eat, sleep, repeat. Look at how little your days differ.

quotes.text: Would you not think him an utter fool who wept because he was not alive a thousand years ago? And is he not just as much of a fool who weeps because he will not be alive a thousand years from now?
quotes.plain: Grieving that you were not born earlier is as silly as grieving that you will not live later.

quotes.text: No journey but has its end.
quotes.plain: Everything you are travelling toward ends.

quotes.text: You wish to live; well, do you know how to live? You are afraid to die. But come now: is this life of yours anything but death?
quotes.plain: Wanting more life is cheap. Are you actually living the one you have?

quotes.text: There is no life that is not short.
quotes.plain: Every life is short. Stop measuring it against longer ones.

quotes.text: It is with life as it is with a play, it matters not how long the action is spun out, but how good the acting is.
quotes.plain: Length is not the point. How well you play it is.

quotes.text: Nothing, my excellent Lucilius, refreshes and aids a sick man so much as the affection of his friends; nothing so steals away the expectation and the fear of death.
quotes.plain: Nothing heals a sick man like the people who love him.

quotes.text: There is no sorrow in the world, when we have escaped from the fear of death.
quotes.plain: Lose the fear of dying and most of your sorrows have nothing to hold onto.

quotes.text: You will die, not because you are ill, but because you are alive; even when you have been cured, the same end awaits you; when you have recovered, it will be not death, but ill-health, that you have escaped.
quotes.plain: You die because you are alive. Getting well only delays it.

quotes.text: No man can suffer both severely and for a long time; Nature, who loves us most tenderly, has so constituted us as to make pain either endurable or short.
quotes.plain: Pain is either bearable or brief. It cannot be both unbearable and endless.

quotes.text: Pain is slight if opinion has added nothing to it; but if, on the other hand, you begin to encourage yourself and say, “It is nothing, a trifling matter at most; keep a stout heart and it will soon cease”; then in thinking it slight, you will make it slight.
quotes.plain: Do not pile commentary on the pain. Call it small and it shrinks.

quotes.text: Everything depends on opinion; ambition, luxury, greed, hark back to opinion. It is according to opinion that we suffer. A man is as wretched as he has convinced himself that he is.
quotes.plain: Your suffering follows what you tell yourself about it.

quotes.text: What benefit is there in reviewing past sufferings, and in being unhappy, just because once you were unhappy?
quotes.plain: Replaying old pain just makes you hurt twice.

quotes.text: Two elements must therefore be rooted out once for all, the fear of future suffering, and the recollection of past suffering; since the latter no longer concerns me, and the former concerns me not yet.
quotes.plain: The past hurt is over and the future hurt has not come. Drop both.

quotes.text: Is it for this purpose that we are strong, that we may have light burdens to bear?
quotes.plain: Strength exists to carry heavy things. Do not ask for light ones.

quotes.text: Be your own spectator; seek your own applause.
quotes.plain: Do the hard thing for your own eyes. You are the audience that counts.

quotes.text: “A single day among the learned lasts longer than the longest life of the ignorant.”
quotes.plain: One day used well outweighs a lifetime wasted.

quotes.text: Meanwhile, hold fast to this thought, and grip it close: yield not to adversity; trust not to prosperity; keep before your eyes the full scope of Fortune’s power, as if she would surely do whatever is in her power to do.
quotes.plain: Do not fold under hardship or relax in good times. Expect fortune to do her worst.

quotes.text: Fame is the shadow of virtue; it will attend virtue even against her will.
quotes.plain: Do the work right and recognition follows without you chasing it.

quotes.text: How long did men believe Democritus to be mad! Glory barely came to Socrates.
quotes.plain: The greats were doubted and ignored while they lived.

quotes.text: That man is born merely for a few, who thinks only of the people of his own generation.
quotes.plain: Do not build only for the people around you now.

quotes.text: Pretence accomplishes nothing. Few are deceived by a mask that is easily drawn over the face. Truth is the same in every part.
quotes.plain: Fakes get seen through. Truth holds together everywhere.

quotes.text: How many men, I say to myself, train their bodies, and how few train their minds!
quotes.plain: Everyone trains the body. Almost nobody trains the mind.

quotes.text: All that goes to make you a good man lies within yourself. And what do you need in order to become good? To wish it.
quotes.plain: Becoming good costs nothing but wanting it.

quotes.text: First of all, free yourself from the fear of death, for death puts the yoke about our necks; then free yourself from the fear of poverty.
quotes.plain: Two fears keep people leashed: dying and going broke.

quotes.text: If you would know how little evil there is in poverty, compare the faces of the poor with those of the rich; the poor man smiles more often and more genuinely; his troubles do not go deep down; even if any anxiety comes upon him, it passes like a fitful cloud.
quotes.plain: Poor people often laugh more. Their worries pass quickly.

quotes.text: If you wish to set a value on yourself, put away your money, your estates, your honours, and look into your own soul. At present, you are taking the word of others for what you are.
quotes.plain: Strip away money and titles and look at the person. Do not let others set your price.

quotes.text: In order to discover one grateful person, it is worth while to make trial of many ungrateful ones.
quotes.plain: Most people won't be grateful. Helping a lot of them to find the one who is can still be worth it.

quotes.text: After a shipwreck, sailors try the sea again. The banker is not frightened away from the forum by the swindler.
quotes.plain: One loss is no reason to quit the sea.

quotes.text: My master Attalus used to say: “Evil herself drinks the largest portion of her own poison.”
quotes.plain: Doing wrong hurts the wrongdoer most.

quotes.text: And what is more wretched than a man who forgets his benefits and clings to his injuries?
quotes.plain: Holding grudges while forgetting kindness makes you miserable.

quotes.text: We hold nothing dearer than a benefit, so long as we are seeking one; we hold nothing cheaper after we have received it.
quotes.plain: We crave favors until we get them, then forget them.

quotes.text: We consider not what we have obtained, but what we are to seek.
quotes.plain: Greed looks at what is next and ignores what it already has.

quotes.text: I hold that he who lies on a perfumed couch is no less dead than he who is dragged along by the executioner’s hook.
quotes.plain: A soft life of ease is a slow way of being dead.

quotes.text: Leisure without study is death; it is a tomb for the living man.
quotes.plain: Rest with no growth in it is a tomb.

quotes.text: As if the real causes of our anxieties did not follow us across the seas!
quotes.plain: Running away does not work. Your worries travel with you.

quotes.text: Fortune has not the long reach with which we credit her; she can seize none except him that clings to her.
quotes.plain: Luck can only take what you are gripping. Hold your possessions loosely.

quotes.text: It is not pain that we praise, it is the man whom pain has not coerced. One praises not death, but the man whose soul death takes away before it can confound it.
quotes.plain: We admire the person who stays steady through hardship, not the hardship.

quotes.text: The soul must be hardened by long practice, so that it may learn to endure the sight and the approach of death.
quotes.plain: Courage is trained slowly by facing hard things on purpose.

quotes.text: When truth is at stake, we must act more frankly; and when fear is to be combated, we must act more bravely.
quotes.plain: Speak plainly and meet fear head on.

quotes.text: “Fellow-soldiers, let us to our breakfast, knowing that we shall sup in Hades!”
quotes.plain: Leonidas told his men to eat well, since they would dine in the underworld.

quotes.text: I shall keep watching myself continually, and, a most useful habit, shall review each day.
quotes.plain: Audit your own day, every day.

quotes.text: Drunkenness kindles and discloses every kind of vice, and removes the sense of shame that veils our evil undertakings.
quotes.plain: Drink does not make you worse, it takes away the shame that was holding you back.

quotes.text: Do that which is easiest of all, namely, demonstrate that what men call pleasures are punishments as soon as they have exceeded due bounds.
quotes.plain: Any pleasure past its limit turns into punishment.

quotes.text: Abandon riches, which are either a danger or a burden to the possessor. Abandon the pleasures of the body and of the mind; they only soften and weaken you.
quotes.plain: Money is a danger or a burden. Comfort makes you soft.

quotes.text: Abandon your quest for office; it is a swollen, idle, and empty thing, a thing that has no goal, as anxious to see no one outstrip it as to see no one at its heels.
quotes.plain: Chasing rank is empty, a race with no finish line.

quotes.text: Vices are never genuinely tamed.
quotes.plain: A bad habit stays wild underneath. Do not trust yourself with it.

quotes.text: How have I the power to bring something to a close, when I have not had the power to check it at the beginning? For it is easier to keep a thing out than to keep it under after you have let it in.
quotes.plain: Easier to keep a habit out than to master it once it is in.

quotes.text: It is proper for him to be careful, but not to be fearful.
quotes.plain: Be careful, not afraid.

quotes.text: Liberty is lost unless we despise those things which put the yoke upon our necks.
quotes.plain: You are free only if you can do without the things that control you.

quotes.text: Because of his poverty he is prevented from showing how the State should be handled; but he teaches, none the less, how poverty should be handled.
quotes.plain: Being broke does not stop you from showing how to handle it well.

quotes.text: Pain, want, disgrace, imprisonment, exile, these are universally to be feared; but when they encounter the wise man, they are tamed.
quotes.plain: The scariest things stop being scary once you can handle them.

quotes.text: We have become so luxurious that we will have nothing but precious stones to walk upon.
quotes.plain: Comfort keeps demanding more until nothing is enough.

quotes.text: We old men must learn this precept; for there is none of us who is not planting an olive-yard for his successor.
quotes.plain: Plant trees whose shade you will never sit in.

quotes.text: He who blushes at riding in a rattle-trap will boast when he rides in style.
quotes.plain: If you feel shame in a beat-up ride, you will brag in a fancy one. Both are about other people's eyes.

quotes.text: Neither master nor mule is improved by such trappings.
quotes.plain: Nice stuff does not improve the owner.

quotes.text: Money tumbles into the hands of certain men as a shilling tumbles down a sewer.
quotes.plain: Plenty of rich people got it by luck, not merit.

quotes.text: Why, then, is the wise man great? Because he has a great soul.
quotes.plain: Greatness is in the soul, not in what you own.

quotes.text: Those things which are goods produce confidence, but riches produce shamelessness. The things which are goods give us greatness of soul, but riches give us arrogance. And arrogance is nothing else than a false show of greatness.
quotes.plain: Wealth makes people arrogant, which is greatness faked.

quotes.text: Pronouncing syllables, investigating words, memorizing plays, or making rules for the scansion of poetry, what is there in all this that rids one of fear, roots out desire, or bridles the passions?
quotes.plain: Knowing a lot of trivia does nothing about your fear or your cravings. Study what changes you.

quotes.text: You are showing me what the doleful keys are; show me rather how, in the midst of adversity, I may keep from uttering a doleful note.
quotes.plain: Skip the theory. Teach me how to stay steady when things go bad.

quotes.text: The mathematician teaches me how I may lose none of my boundaries; I, however, seek to learn how to lose them all with a light heart.
quotes.plain: Learn to lose things without it wrecking you.

quotes.text: You know what a straight line is; but how does it benefit you if you do not know what is straight in this life of ours?
quotes.plain: Smart about everything except how to live is not smart.

quotes.text: I, for my part, do not know what is to be, but I do know what may come to be. I shall have no misgivings in this matter; I await the future in its entirety; and if there is any abatement in its severity, I make the most of it.
quotes.plain: You can't know what's coming, but you can be ready for all of it. Take any mercy as a bonus.

quotes.text: I am ready for favourable events in every case, but I am prepared for evil.
quotes.plain: Hope for the good, plan for the bad.

quotes.text: Bravery is a scorner of things which inspire fear; it looks down upon, challenges, and crushes the powers of terror and all that would drive our freedom under the yoke.
quotes.plain: Courage means staring down what scares you until it loses its hold.

quotes.text: Temperance knows that the best measure of the appetites is not what you want to take, but what you ought to take.
quotes.plain: Measure yourself by what you should have, not what you want.

quotes.text: Let all other things be driven out, and let the breast be emptied to receive virtue.
quotes.plain: Clear out the clutter to make room for what matters.

quotes.text: Come now, do not tell me that life is long!
quotes.plain: Life is short. Stop spending it on junk.

quotes.text: Medicine begins to do good at the time when a touch makes the diseased body tingle with pain.
quotes.plain: The truth stings because it's starting to work.

quotes.text: At times you should allow words other than compliments to reach your ears, and because as individuals you are unwilling to hear the truth, hear it collectively.
quotes.plain: Let people tell you what you don't want to hear.

quotes.text: An estate which held a nation is too narrow for a single lord.
quotes.plain: Greed never reaches a point where it feels like enough.

quotes.text: What profit to you are your many bed-chambers? You sleep in one.
quotes.plain: You can only use so much. The rest is for show.

quotes.text: Poor wretches, do you not know that your appetites are bigger than your bellies?
quotes.plain: You want far more than you can ever enjoy.

quotes.text: Study, not in order to add anything to your knowledge, but to make your knowledge better.
quotes.plain: Learn to improve how you live, not to pile up facts.

quotes.text: Who can doubt, my dear Lucilius, that life is the gift of the immortal gods, but that living well is the gift of philosophy?
quotes.plain: Being alive is given. Living well you have to learn.

quotes.text: A thatched roof once covered free men; under marble and gold dwells slavery.
quotes.plain: The more luxury you need, the less free you are.

quotes.text: Fool that I am, to have been carrying superfluous baggage all this time!
quotes.plain: Look at what you carry around and drop whatever you don't need.

quotes.text: The things that are indispensable require no elaborate pains for their acquisition; it is only the luxuries that call for labour.
quotes.plain: What you truly need is cheap. The hard grind is for extras.

quotes.text: All things were ready for us at our birth; it is we that have made everything difficult for ourselves, through our disdain for what is easy.
quotes.plain: Most of the struggle is self-made by refusing the simple route.

quotes.text: It was avarice that introduced poverty and, by craving much, lost all.
quotes.plain: Wanting everything is how people end up with nothing.

quotes.text: Care vexes us in our purple, and routs us from our beds with the sharpest of goads; but how soft was the sleep the hard earth bestowed upon the men of that day!
quotes.plain: Comfort brings worry. People on hard beds slept better.

quotes.text: Virtue is not vouchsafed to a soul unless that soul has been trained and taught, and by unremitting practice brought to perfection.
quotes.plain: Being good is a skill. It takes daily reps.

quotes.text: Strangeness adds to the weight of calamities, and every mortal feels the greater pain as a result of that which also brings surprise.
quotes.plain: Surprise makes bad news hit harder. Expect the hit and it weighs less.

quotes.text: Our minds should be sent forward in advance to meet all problems, and we should consider, not what is wont to happen, but what can happen.
quotes.plain: Rehearse the worst case before it shows up.

quotes.text: No time is exempt; in the midst of our very pleasures there spring up causes of suffering.
quotes.plain: Good times don't protect you. Stay ready.

quotes.text: It would be some consolation for the feebleness of our selves and our works, if all things should perish as slowly as they come into being; but as it is, increases are of sluggish growth, but the way to ruin is rapid.
quotes.plain: Building is slow and falling is fast, so guard what you build.

quotes.text: Nothing, whether public or private, is stable; the destinies of men, no less than those of cities, are in a whirl.
quotes.plain: Nothing stays put. Plan for change.

quotes.text: Let us rise, therefore, to confront the operations of Fortune, and whatever happens, let us have the assurance that it is not so great as rumour advertises it to be.
quotes.plain: Whatever hits you is never as big as the hype around it.

quotes.text: It would be tedious to recount all the ways by which fate may come; but this one thing I know: all the works of mortal man have been doomed to mortality, and in the midst of things which have been destined to die, we live!
quotes.plain: Everything made dies. We live anyway, so live fully.
