quotes.text: Oftentimes a reverse has but made room for more prosperous fortune. Many structures have fallen only to rise to a greater height.
quotes.plain: A loss can clear the ground for something bigger.

quotes.text: We are unequal at birth, but are equal in death.
quotes.plain: Death levels everyone, rich or poor.

quotes.text: I cannot give anything easier to any man, but whoever wishes will make things easier for himself.
quotes.plain: Life won't get softer. Your attitude can.

quotes.text: You must suffer pain, and thirst, and hunger, and old age too, if a longer stay among men shall be granted you; you must be sick, and you must suffer loss and death.
quotes.plain: Hardship comes with being alive. Don't be shocked by it.

quotes.text: For me the talk of ignorant men is like the rumblings which issue from the belly.
quotes.plain: Noise from fools is just noise.

quotes.text: What madness it is to be afraid of disrepute in the judgment of the disreputable!
quotes.plain: Why fear the opinion of people you don't respect?

quotes.text: That man, I declare, is happy whom nothing makes less strong than he is; he keeps to the heights, leaning upon none but himself; for one who sustains himself by any prop may fall.
quotes.plain: Lean on yourself. Anything else you depend on can give way.

quotes.text: What is the happy life? It is peace of mind, and lasting tranquillity.
quotes.plain: Happiness is a calm mind that lasts.

quotes.text: The scabbard does not make the sword good or bad.
quotes.plain: Packaging doesn't change what you are.

quotes.text: Disasters, therefore, and losses, and wrongs, have only the same power over virtue that a cloud has over the sun.
quotes.plain: Bad luck can dim you but can't put you out.

quotes.text: If virtue only stands her ground, she cannot be driven from the field; she must either conquer or be conquered.
quotes.plain: Hold your ground and you can't be pushed off it.

quotes.text: The soul, I affirm, knows that riches are stored elsewhere than in men’s heaped-up treasure-houses; that it is the soul, and not the strong-box, which should be filled.
quotes.plain: Fill yourself up, not the vault.

quotes.text: We should strive, not to live long, but to live rightly; for to achieve long life you have need of Fate only, but for right living you need the soul.
quotes.plain: Length of life is luck. Quality is up to you.

quotes.text: Pray, let us see to it, my dear Lucilius, that our lives, like jewels of great price, be noteworthy not because of their width but because of their weight. Let us measure them by their performance, not by their duration.
quotes.plain: Judge a life by what it did, not how long it ran.

quotes.text: Just as one of small stature can be a perfect man, so a life of small compass can be a perfect life.
quotes.plain: A short life can still be complete.

quotes.text: How long I am to exist is not mine to decide, but how long I shall go on existing in my present way is in my own control.
quotes.plain: You can't pick your lifespan. You can pick how you live.

quotes.text: This is the only thing you have the right to require of me, that I shall cease to measure out an inglorious age as it were in darkness, and devote myself to living instead of being carried along past life.
quotes.plain: Stop drifting through the years. Actually live them.

quotes.text: And what, you ask, is the fullest span of life? It is living until you possess wisdom.
quotes.plain: A full life is one where you've learned how to live.

quotes.text: And anyhow, what does it matter for how long a time you avoid that which you cannot escape?
quotes.plain: Delaying the inevitable doesn't beat it.

quotes.text: We miss much that is set before our very eyes.
quotes.plain: A lot of what you need is already in front of you. You just miss it.

quotes.text: Buy not what you need, but what you must have. That which you do not need, is dear even at a farthing.
quotes.plain: Anything you don't need is expensive, even if it's cheap.

quotes.text: Fortune favours the brave, but the coward is foiled by his faint heart.
quotes.plain: Nerve gets rewarded. Fear gets you beat.

quotes.text: Nothing is more successful in bringing honourable influences to bear upon the mind, or in straightening out the wavering spirit that is prone to evil, than association with good men.
quotes.plain: Your circle shapes you more than willpower does.

quotes.text: Nobody confines his mistakes to himself; people sprinkle folly among their neighbours, and receive it from them in turn.
quotes.plain: Bad habits spread between people. Choose who you're around.

quotes.text: If you would wield a command that is profitable to yourself, and injurious to nobody, clear your own faults out of the way.
quotes.plain: Fix yourself before you try to lead.

quotes.text: You need never believe that a man can become happy through the unhappiness of another.
quotes.plain: Climbing over people never makes you happy.

quotes.text: Who puts on the purple robe for the sake of flaunting it in no man’s eyes? Who uses gold plate when he dines alone?
quotes.plain: Most flexing is for an audience.

quotes.text: You can make us cease to crave, if you only make us cease to display.
quotes.plain: Cut the audience and the wanting fades.

quotes.text: Ambition, luxury, and waywardness need a stage to act upon; you will cure all those ills if you seek retirement.
quotes.plain: Pull back from the crowd and the urges quiet down.

quotes.text: That which others think elevated, is to them a sheer precipice.
quotes.plain: What looks like a high position from below feels like a cliff edge to the person standing on it.

quotes.text: It is prosperity that takes away righteousness.
quotes.plain: Comfort makes people soft and careless.

quotes.text: We often want one thing and pray for another, not telling the truth even to the gods, while the gods either do not hearken, or else take pity on us.
quotes.plain: We aren't honest even with ourselves about what we want.

quotes.text: You need not wonder that diseases are beyond counting: count the cooks!
quotes.plain: Excess feeds the problem. Count the indulgences.

quotes.text: We are mad, not only individually, but nationally.
quotes.plain: The craziness isn't just personal. It's everywhere.

quotes.text: Deeds that would be punished by loss of life when committed in secret, are praised by us because uniformed generals have carried them out.
quotes.plain: People call it fine as long as the right people do it.

quotes.text: The same act may be either shameful or honourable: the purpose and the manner make all the difference.
quotes.plain: Same action, different intent, different worth.

quotes.text: We must set before our eyes the goal of the Supreme Good, towards which we may strive, and to which all our acts and words may have reference, just as sailors must guide their course according to a certain star.
quotes.plain: Pick a north star and steer by it.

quotes.text: Life without ideals is erratic: as soon as an ideal is to be set up, doctrines begin to be necessary.
quotes.plain: Without a guiding principle you zigzag. Pick one.

quotes.text: I am sure you will admit that there is nothing more shameful than uncertain and wavering conduct, than the habit of timorous retreat.
quotes.plain: Flip-flopping and backing off is the real disgrace.

quotes.text: Would you win over the gods? Then be a good man. Whoever imitates them, is worshipping them sufficiently.
quotes.plain: Want to honor what is higher than you? Just be a good person.

quotes.text: What a little thing it is not to harm one whom you ought to help!
quotes.plain: Not hurting people is the bare minimum.

quotes.text: Our relations with one another are like a stone arch, which would collapse if the stones did not mutually support each other, and which is upheld in this very way.
quotes.plain: People hold each other up or everyone falls.

quotes.text: Let us banish rumour and set a value upon each thing, asking what it is and not what it is called.
quotes.plain: Judge things by what they are, not their reputation.

quotes.text: Peace of mind is enjoyed only by those who have attained a fixed and unchanging standard of judgment; the rest of mankind continually ebb and flow in their decisions, floating in a condition where they alternately reject things and seek them.
quotes.plain: Calm comes from standards that don't shift with every mood.

quotes.text: If you would always desire the same things, you must desire the truth.
quotes.plain: Chase what's true and your wants stop flipping.

quotes.text: If you ask me, I think that for a man there is no misery unless there be something in the universe which he thinks miserable.
quotes.plain: Things only wreck you if you decide they do.

quotes.text: A long life includes all these troubles, just as a long journey includes dust and mud and rain.
quotes.plain: You asked for a long life, so you asked for the hard parts too.

quotes.text: The road to vice is not only downhill, but steep; and many men are rendered incorrigible by the fact that, while in all other crafts errors bring shame to good craftsmen and cause vexation to those who go astray, the errors of life are a positive source of pleasure.
quotes.plain: Bad habits feel good while you do them, which is why they are so hard to quit.

quotes.text: A good conscience, however, wishes to come forth and be seen of men; wickedness fears the very shadows.
quotes.plain: If you are proud of what you do, you have nothing to hide.

quotes.text: Good luck frees many men from punishment, but no man from fear.
quotes.plain: You can get away with it and still never relax.

quotes.text: You need never believe that anyone who depends upon happiness is happy!
quotes.plain: If your joy depends on things outside you, it is not really yours.

quotes.text: It is tragic for the soul to be apprehensive of the future and wretched in anticipation of wretchedness, consumed with an anxious desire that the objects which give pleasure may remain in its possession to the very end.
quotes.plain: Dreading the loss of what you have wrecks the enjoyment of having it.

quotes.text: And there is no difference between grief for something lost and the fear of losing it.
quotes.plain: Fearing a loss already hurts like the loss.

quotes.text: He who can bear Fortune, can also beware of Fortune.
quotes.plain: If you can take a hit, you are better at dodging one.

quotes.text: And there is nothing more wretched or foolish than premature fear. What madness it is to anticipate one’s troubles!
quotes.plain: Stop suffering in advance for things that may never happen.

quotes.text: We must lose our lives as surely as we lose our property, and this, if we understand the truth, is itself a consolation. Lose it with equanimity; for you must lose your life also.
quotes.plain: You will lose everything anyway, so lose things calmly.

quotes.text: To have may be taken from us, to have had, never.
quotes.plain: What you had and enjoyed cannot be undone.

quotes.text: Chance robs us of the thing, but leaves us its use and its enjoyment, and we have lost this if we are so unfair as to regret.
quotes.plain: Luck takes the thing but not the good you got from it, unless you waste that on regret.

quotes.text: Pain he endures, death he awaits.
quotes.plain: Take pain head on and meet death calmly.

quotes.text: The past is ours, and there is nothing more secure for us than that which has been.
quotes.plain: Nobody can take back what already happened to you.

quotes.text: Whoever complains about the death of anyone, is complaining that he was a man.
quotes.plain: Griefing that people die is arguing with being human.

quotes.text: Periods of time separate us, but death levels us.
quotes.plain: Age and rank separate us for now, death makes us equal.

quotes.text: Everything is slippery, treacherous, and more shifting than any weather.
quotes.plain: Nothing stays put, so do not build on it staying the same.

quotes.text: And yet all men complain about the one thing wherein none of them is deceived.
quotes.plain: Death is the one promise life keeps, and we still complain.

quotes.text: Life is neither a Good nor an Evil; it is simply the place where good and evil exist.
quotes.plain: Life is the arena, not the verdict. What you do in it decides.

quotes.text: Yours is not pain; it is a mere sting, and it is you yourself who are turning it into pain.
quotes.plain: A lot of what you call suffering is you inflating a small hit.

quotes.text: The display of grief makes more demands than grief itself: how few men are sad in their own company!
quotes.plain: Much of our show of pain is for the audience.

quotes.text: O what madness it is to plot out far-reaching hopes!
quotes.plain: Do not stake your whole life on a future you do not own.

quotes.text: No one has any right to draw for himself upon the future.
quotes.plain: Tomorrow is not yours to spend yet.

quotes.text: Time does indeed roll along by fixed law, but as in darkness; and what is it to me whether Nature’s course is sure, when my own is unsure?
quotes.plain: Time keeps its schedule, but you do not know yours.

quotes.text: Let us postpone nothing. Let us balance life’s account every day.
quotes.plain: Close out each day as if it could be the last.

quotes.text: The greatest flaw in life is that it is always imperfect, and that a certain part of it is postponed.
quotes.plain: The thing that ruins a life is putting parts of it off.

quotes.text: We must get rid of this craving for life, and learn that it makes no difference when your suffering comes, because at some time you are bound to suffer.
quotes.plain: Suffering is coming either way, so stop bargaining for more time.

quotes.text: The point is, not how long you live, but how nobly you live.
quotes.plain: Length of life matters less than how you live it.

quotes.text: Nothing has corrupted oratory and all other studies that depend on hearing so much as popular approval.
quotes.plain: Chasing applause ruins the work.

quotes.text: Survey everything that lies about you, as if it were luggage in a guest-chamber: you must travel on.
quotes.plain: You are a guest here. Hold your stuff loosely.

quotes.text: Nature strips you as bare at your departure as at your entrance.
quotes.plain: You leave with nothing, same as you came.

quotes.text: That day, which you fear as being the end of all things, is the birthday of your eternity.
quotes.plain: The day you dread may be a beginning.

quotes.text: Why are you looking about for troubles which may perhaps come your way, but which may indeed not come your way at all?
quotes.plain: You are scanning for disasters that probably will not arrive.

quotes.text: A man may be wise without parade and without arousing enmity.
quotes.plain: Be good at what you do quietly.

quotes.text: Your ambition will be so frenzied that you will regard yourself last in the race if there is anyone in front of you.
quotes.plain: Comparison makes you feel poor and behind no matter how far you have come.

quotes.text: Regard everything that pleases you as if it were a flourishing plant; make the most of it while it is in leaf, for different plants at different seasons must fall and die.
quotes.plain: Enjoy what you have while it is green.

quotes.text: Others are snatched from sight; we ourselves are being stealthily filched away from ourselves.
quotes.plain: You are changing and losing time every day too, you just do not see it.

quotes.text: If you are wise, mingle these two elements: do not hope without despair, or despair without hope.
quotes.plain: Expect the worst while hoping for the best, and never fully either one.

quotes.text: It is medicine, not scenery, for which the sick man must go a-searching.
quotes.plain: A change of scenery will not heal what is wrong with you.

quotes.text: That from which you are running, is within you.
quotes.plain: What you are running from travels with you.

quotes.text: The only harbour safe from the seething storms of this life is scorn of the future, a firm stand, a readiness to receive Fortune’s missiles full in the breast, neither skulking nor turning the back.
quotes.plain: Safety is stopping fearing what comes and standing your ground.

quotes.text: Many a sight that is held a terror in the night-time, is turned to ridicule by day.
quotes.plain: Fears shrink once you look at them in daylight.

quotes.text: Our lack of confidence is not the result of difficulty; the difficulty comes from our lack of confidence.
quotes.plain: It is not hard, you just doubt yourself.

quotes.text: If you set a high value on liberty, you must set a low value on everything else.
quotes.plain: Freedom costs you the need for stuff.

quotes.text: You will escape envy if you do not force yourself upon the public view, if you do not boast your possessions, if you understand how to enjoy things privately.
quotes.plain: Do not flaunt it and people will leave you alone.

quotes.text: Nothing, however, will help you so much as keeping still, talking very little with others, and as much as may be with yourself.
quotes.plain: Talk less, and spend time with your own thoughts.

quotes.text: The most important contribution to peace of mind is never to do wrong.
quotes.plain: A clean conscience is the first step to calm.

quotes.text: Whoever expects punishment, receives it, but whoever deserves it, expects it.
quotes.plain: If you did wrong, you will spend your days waiting for the hit.

quotes.text: No man is at the mercy of affairs. He gets entangled in them of his own accord, and then flatters himself that being busy is a proof of happiness.
quotes.plain: Being busy is a choice, and it is not the same as being happy.

quotes.text: Just as we suffer from excess in all things, so we suffer from excess in literature; thus we learn our lessons, not for life, but for the lecture-room.
quotes.plain: Do not study to sound smart. Learn to live.

quotes.text: Life is not a dainty business.
quotes.plain: Life is rough, so expect that.

quotes.text: You have started on a long journey; you are bound to slip, collide, fall, become weary, and cry out: “O for Death!”, or in other words, tell lies.
quotes.plain: You will fall and want to quit. Expect it and do not mean it.

quotes.text: Everyone approaches courageously a danger which he has prepared himself to meet long before, and withstands even hardships if he has previously practised how to meet them.
quotes.plain: Rehearse the hard thing ahead of time and it loses its power.

quotes.text: Whatever happens, assume that it was bound to happen, and do not be willing to rail at Nature.
quotes.plain: It was always going to happen, so stop fighting reality.

quotes.text: Let us live thus, and speak thus; let Fate find us ready and alert.
quotes.plain: Be ready when it hits.

quotes.text: Absorb not all that you wish, but all that you can hold.
quotes.plain: Take on only what you can carry.

quotes.text: The poor lack much; the greedy man lacks all.
quotes.plain: Greed leaves you with nothing, no matter how much you have.

quotes.text: Let every day, as soon as it comes, be welcome as being the choicest, and let it be made our own possession. We must catch that which flees.
quotes.plain: Grab each day, because it is leaving.

quotes.text: We should so learn them that words may become deeds.
quotes.plain: Only learning that turns into action counts.

quotes.text: One must steer, not talk.
quotes.plain: Do the work, do not talk about it.

quotes.text: I shall show you how men can prove their words to be their own: it is by doing what they have been talking about.
quotes.plain: Your words are yours only when you act on them.

quotes.text: None of us has sifted out the truth; we have passed fear on to one another; none has dared to approach the object which caused his dread, and to understand the nature of his fear, aye, the good behind it.
quotes.plain: Most fear is inherited and never examined.

quotes.text: What is necessary will meet you everywhere; what is superfluous has always to be hunted out, and with great endeavour.
quotes.plain: What you need is easy to find. Wants take a long chase.

quotes.text: The time to admire your own conduct is when you have come to despise the necessities.
quotes.plain: Giving up luxuries is easy. Mastery is not needing the basics.

quotes.text: I came to despise riches, not because of their uselessness, but because of their pettiness.
quotes.plain: Wealth is not evil, it is small.

quotes.text: Why wonder? Why gape in astonishment? It is all show; such things are displayed, not possessed; while they please they pass away.
quotes.plain: Flashy wealth is for show and it fades.

quotes.text: If you are willing to think often of these things, you will strive not to seem happy, but to be happy, and, in addition, to seem happy to yourself rather than to others.
quotes.plain: Be happy for real, not for show.

quotes.text: Men love and hate their vices at the same time.
quotes.plain: You can hate a habit and still want it.

quotes.text: And what is Bravery? It is the impregnable fortress for our mortal weakness; when a man has surrounded himself therewith, he can hold out free from anxiety during life’s siege; for he is using his own strength and his own weapons.
quotes.plain: Courage is the fort that protects you from everything else.

quotes.text: There are never any occasions when you need think yourself safe because you wield the weapons of Fortune; fight with your own!
quotes.plain: Do not rely on luck or borrowed advantages. Build your own.

quotes.text: Self-Command is the greatest command of all.
quotes.plain: Ruling yourself is the biggest power there is.

quotes.text: You need not look about for the reward of a just deed; a just deed in itself offers a still greater return.
quotes.plain: Doing right is its own payment.

quotes.text: Those who wish their virtue to be advertised are not striving for virtue but for renown.
quotes.plain: Doing good for applause is chasing fame, not goodness.

quotes.text: Show me any man, however famous; I can tell you what it was that his age forgave in him, and what it was that his age purposely overlooked.
quotes.plain: Every famous person has flaws the crowd chose to ignore. Nobody you admire is clean.

quotes.text: When the soul is sound and strong, the style too is vigorous, energetic, manly; but if the soul lose its balance, down comes all the rest in ruins.
quotes.plain: Everything you do and say rests on how steady your mind is. Lose that and the rest falls apart.

quotes.text: The soul is our king. If it be safe, the other functions remain on duty and serve with obedience; but the slightest lack of equilibrium in the soul causes them to waver along with it.
quotes.plain: Your mind runs the whole operation. When it wobbles, your habits and your work wobble with it.

quotes.text: Now is it not madness, Lucilius, for none of us to reflect that he is mortal? Or frail? Or again that he is but one individual?
quotes.plain: You will die, you are fragile, and you are only one person. Act like you know it.

quotes.text: You should seek what to write, rather than how to write it, and even that not for the purpose of writing but of feeling it, that you may thus make what you have felt more your own and, as it were, set a seal on it.
quotes.plain: Care about what you actually feel and think, not how polished it sounds. Make it yours first.

quotes.text: The really great man speaks informally and easily; whatever he says, he speaks with assurance rather than with pains.
quotes.plain: Real confidence sounds relaxed. Straining to impress is a sign you are not sure.

quotes.text: Style is the garb of thought: if it be trimmed, or dyed, or treated, it shows that there are defects and a certain amount of flaws in the mind.
quotes.plain: Over-polish is a cover for weakness underneath.

quotes.text: We cheat our own eyesight, and when we have overlaid our ceilings with gold, what else is it but a lie in which we take such delight?
quotes.plain: We love the gilding on things we know are cheap wood underneath. Wealth is often a nice-looking lie.

quotes.text: What tears and toil does money wring from us! Greed is wretched in that which it craves and wretched in that which it wins!
quotes.plain: Chasing money hurts, and having more of it does not stop the hurt.

quotes.text: The possession of riches means even greater agony of spirit than the acquisition of riches.
quotes.plain: Getting rich is stressful. Keeping it is worse.

quotes.text: Men complain about their plans and the outcome of their plans; they always prefer what they have failed to win.
quotes.plain: People are never happy with what they have. What they missed always looks better.

quotes.text: There is no vice which lacks some plea; there is no vice that at the start is not modest and easily entreated; but afterwards the trouble spreads more widely.
quotes.plain: Every bad habit starts small and reasonable. It always grows.

quotes.text: Every emotion at the start is weak. Afterwards, it rouses itself and gains strength by progress; it is more easy to forestall it than to forgo it.
quotes.plain: Stop it at the first spark. Quitting it later is much harder than never letting it start.

quotes.text: In so far as we are able, let us step back from slippery places; even on dry ground it is hard enough to take a sturdy stand.
quotes.plain: Stay away from situations that tempt you. Standing firm is hard enough without them.

quotes.text: And do you know why we have not the power to attain this Stoic ideal? It is because we refuse to believe in our power.
quotes.plain: You are not weak. You just do not believe you can do it.

quotes.text: We mortals have been endowed with sufficient strength by nature, if only we use this strength, if only we concentrate our powers and rouse them all to help us or at least not to hinder us. The reason is unwillingness, the excuse, inability.
quotes.plain: You have enough strength. When you say you cannot, you mean you will not.

quotes.text: I think nothing is baser than to pray for death.
quotes.plain: Wishing you were dead is the lowest move there is. Stay and fight it out.

quotes.text: How foolish it is to practise strokes after you have heard the signal for the fight! Away with all these dummy-weapons; you need armour for a fight to the finish.
quotes.plain: Stop rehearsing. The fight has started, so go do the real thing.

quotes.text: Nature has not given us such a generous and free-handed space of time that we can have the leisure to waste any of it.
quotes.plain: There is not enough time to waste any of it.

quotes.text: Out of this time, so short and swift, that carries us away in its flight, of what avail is it to spend the greater part on useless things?
quotes.plain: Life is short and fast. Why give most of it to things that do not matter?

quotes.text: Make me braver, make me calmer, make me the equal of Fortune, make me her superior.
quotes.plain: Wisdom is only worth it if it makes you braver and calmer than whatever life throws at you.

quotes.text: Happiness is not, as men think, a greedy thing; it is a lowly thing; for that reason it never gluts a man’s desire.
quotes.plain: Happiness is simple and small. That is why more stuff never satisfies the hunger for it.

quotes.text: You deem lofty the objects you seek, because you are on a low level and hence far away from them; but they are mean in the sight of him who has reached them.
quotes.plain: Goals look huge from far away. Once someone has them, they look small.

quotes.text: Most men admire that which deceives them at a distance, and by the crowd good things are supposed to be big things.
quotes.plain: The crowd mistakes big for good. Do not trust what only looks great from far away.

quotes.text: A starving man despises nothing.
quotes.plain: Real need makes everything taste good. Comfort is what makes you picky.

quotes.text: Would you rather have much, or enough? He who has much desires more, a proof that he has not yet acquired enough; but he who has enough has attained that which never fell to the rich man’s lot, a stopping-point.
quotes.plain: The man with a lot always wants more. The man with enough is the only one who gets to stop.

quotes.text: Enough is never too little, and not-enough is never too much.
quotes.plain: If you decide what is enough, you are rich. If you do not, nothing is ever enough.

quotes.text: Money never made a man rich; on the contrary, it always smites men with a greater craving for itself.
quotes.plain: Money does not cure wanting money. It feeds it.

quotes.text: Hunger is not ambitious; it is quite satisfied to come to an end; nor does it care very much what food brings it to an end.
quotes.plain: Your real needs are cheap and easy. It is the extras that cost you.

quotes.text: Carelessness looks like ease, and rashness like bravery.
quotes.plain: Some vices dress up as virtues. Look closely before you admire them.

quotes.text: “Whatever this may be,” he says, “it is my lot; it is rough and it is hard, but I must work diligently at the task.”
quotes.plain: Do not curse what you got dealt. It is hard, so do the work anyway.

quotes.text: Nothing is enough for us, though we must die some day, or rather, are already dying; for we stand daily nearer the brink, and every hour of time thrusts us on towards the precipice over which we must fall.
quotes.plain: We chase more while already dying. Every day brings you closer to the edge.

quotes.text: The failing step does not produce, it merely announces, weariness. The last hour reaches, but every hour approaches, death. Death wears us away, but does not whirl us away.
quotes.plain: Death is not one event at the end. It is every hour wearing you down a little.

quotes.text: It is indeed consistency that abides; false things do not last.
quotes.plain: Only what you do steadily lasts. Fakes fall apart.

quotes.text: The greatest proof of an evil mind is unsteadiness, and continued wavering between pretence of virtue and love of vice.
quotes.plain: Flip-flopping between who you claim to be and who you act like is the clearest sign something is off.

quotes.text: Believe me, it is a great rôle, to play the rôle of one man. But nobody can be one person except the wise man; the rest of us often shift our masks.
quotes.plain: Being the same person every day is rare and hard. Most people swap masks to suit the moment.

quotes.text: You should therefore force yourself to maintain to the very end of life’s drama the character which you assumed at the beginning.
quotes.plain: Pick who you are and stay him all the way to the end.

quotes.text: We are more industrious, and we are better men if we anticipate the day and welcome the dawn; but we are base churls if we lie dozing when the sun is high in the heavens, or if we wake up only when noon arrives; and even then to many it seems not yet dawn.
quotes.plain: Get up early and meet the day. Sleeping through it makes you smaller.

quotes.text: The method of maintaining righteousness is simple; the method of maintaining wickedness is complicated, and has infinite opportunity to swerve.
quotes.plain: Doing right is simple. Doing wrong takes endless upkeep.

quotes.text: If we follow Nature, all is easy and unobstructed; but if we combat Nature, our life differs not a whit from that of men who row against the current.
quotes.plain: Fighting your own nature is rowing upstream. Work with it.

quotes.text: To have whatsoever he wishes is in no man’s power; it is in his power not to wish for what he has not, but cheerfully to employ what comes to him.
quotes.plain: You cannot get everything you want. You can stop wanting what you lack and use what you have.

quotes.text: A great step towards independence is a good-humoured stomach, one that is willing to endure rough treatment.
quotes.plain: Getting comfortable with rough conditions makes you free. Do not need it nice.

quotes.text: How many things are superfluous we fail to realize until they begin to be wanting; we merely used them not because we needed them but because we had them.
quotes.plain: You only find out what you did not need when it is gone. Most of it was habit.

quotes.text: Many of our troubles may be explained from the fact that we live according to a pattern, and, instead of arranging our lives according to reason, are led astray by convention.
quotes.plain: A lot of your stress comes from copying what everyone else does instead of thinking.

quotes.text: There are things which, if done by the few, we should refuse to imitate; yet when the majority have begun to do them, we follow along, just as if anything were more honourable because it is more frequent!
quotes.plain: Popular does not mean right. If only a few did it, you would say no.

quotes.text: It is not easy to rid the memory of a catching tune; it stays with us, lasts on, and comes back from time to time.
quotes.plain: What you hear sticks. Be careful who and what you let into your head.

quotes.text: Let us fight in the opposite fashion: let us retreat from the objects that allure, and rouse ourselves to meet the objects that attack.
quotes.plain: Back away from temptation and run toward the hard thing.

quotes.text: The pleasures take one down hill but one must work upwards toward that which is rough and hard to climb; in the one case let us throw our bodies forward, in the others let us put the check-rein on them.
quotes.plain: Pleasure is downhill and easy. Anything worth it is uphill, so lean in.

quotes.text: No man is good by chance. Virtue is something which must be learned.
quotes.plain: Nobody is good by accident. It is a skill you practice.

quotes.text: Poverty is an evil to no man unless he kick against the goads.
quotes.plain: Being poor only wrecks you if you fight it with resentment.

quotes.text: Death is not an evil; why need you ask? Death alone is the equal privilege of mankind.
quotes.plain: Death is not bad, and it is the one thing everybody gets.

quotes.text: And what is this Good? I shall tell you: it is a free mind, an upright mind, subjecting other things to itself and itself to nothing.
quotes.plain: The best thing is a mind that rules everything else and answers to nothing.

quotes.text: Why, pray, do you foster and practise your bodily strength? Nature has granted strength in greater degree to cattle and wild beasts.
quotes.plain: Animals beat you at strength and looks. Your edge is your mind, so train that most.

quotes.text: You will come to your own when you shall understand that those whom the world calls fortunate are really the most unfortunate of all.
quotes.plain: You have arrived when you stop envying the people everyone calls lucky.

quotes.text: Be thou sure that God acts in like manner: He does not pet the good man: He tries him, hardens him, and fits him for Himself.
quotes.plain: Hard times are not a punishment. They are training for someone worth building.

quotes.text: Is there any hard-working man to whom idleness is not a punishment?
quotes.plain: If you are built to work, sitting around feels like a sentence.

quotes.text: It does not matter what you bear, but how you bear it.
quotes.plain: The hardship is not the test. How you carry it is.

quotes.text: Those who are surfeited with ease break down not only with labour, but with mere motion and by their own weight.
quotes.plain: A soft life makes you collapse at the smallest effort.

quotes.text: Unbroken prosperity cannot bear a single blow; but he who has waged an unceasing strife with his misfortunes has gained a thicker skin by his sufferings, yields to no disaster, and even though he fall yet fights on his knee.
quotes.plain: Easy wins make you fragile. Struggle makes you tough enough to fight from your knees.

quotes.text: Behold a sight worthy to be viewed by a god interested in his own work, behold a pair worthy of a god, a brave man matched with evil fortune, especially if he himself has given the challenge.
quotes.plain: A brave person fighting bad luck, especially one they picked, is the best thing there is to watch.

quotes.text: A gladiator deems it a disgrace to be matched with an inferior, and knows that to win without danger is to win without glory.
quotes.plain: An easy win means nothing. Respect comes from beating something tough.

quotes.text: I think you unhappy because you never have been unhappy: you have passed through your life without meeting an antagonist: no one will know your powers, not even you yourself.
quotes.plain: Without resistance you never learn what you can do, and neither does anyone else.

quotes.text: Valour is greedy of danger, and thinks only of whither it strives to go, not of what it will suffer, since even what it will suffer is part of its glory.
quotes.plain: The brave look at where they are going, not at what it will cost. The cost is part of the story.

quotes.text: Do not, I beg you, dread those things which the immortal gods apply to our minds like spurs: misfortune is virtue’s opportunity.
quotes.plain: Bad luck pushes you forward. It is your chance to prove who you are.

quotes.text: Misfortunes press hardest on those who are unacquainted with them: the yoke feels heavy to the tender neck.
quotes.plain: Hardship crushes the ones who never practiced it.

quotes.text: The recruit turns pale at the thought of a wound: the veteran, who knows that he has often won the victory after losing blood, looks boldly at his own flowing gore.
quotes.plain: Rookies panic at pain. Veterans have bled before and won anyway.

quotes.text: While all excesses are hurtful, excess of comfort is the most hurtful of all; it affects the brain; it leads men’s minds into vain imaginings; it spreads a thick cloud over the boundaries of truth and falsehood.
quotes.plain: Too much comfort rots your thinking more than any other excess.

quotes.text: Fortune lashes and mangles us: well, let us endure it: it is not cruelty, it is a struggle, in which the oftener we engage the braver we shall become.
quotes.plain: Life beating you up is not cruelty, it is a fight. Each round makes you braver.

quotes.text: The strongest part of the body is that which is exercised by the most frequent use: we must entrust ourselves to fortune to be hardened by her against herself: by degrees she will make us a match for herself.
quotes.plain: What you use most gets strongest. Face fate often and she makes you her equal.

quotes.text: Familiarity with danger leads us to despise it.
quotes.plain: The more you face what scares you, the less it scares you.

quotes.text: There is no unhappiness in what use has made part of one’s nature: by degrees men find pleasure in doing what they were first driven to do by necessity.
quotes.plain: What is hard now becomes normal. Keep doing it and you will start to like it.

quotes.text: I am constrained to nothing, I suffer nothing against my will, nor am I God’s slave, but his willing follower, and so much the more because I know that everything is ordained and proceeds according to a law that endures for ever.
quotes.plain: When you accept what happens as your own choice, nothing can force you.

quotes.text: Fire tries gold, misfortune tries brave men.
quotes.plain: Fire shows what gold is. Hard times show who is brave.

quotes.text: It is the part of grovellers and cowards to follow the safe track; courage loves a lofty path.
quotes.plain: Only cowards play it safe. Take the high, hard road.

quotes.text: I have placed every good thing within your own breasts: it is your good fortune not to need any good fortune.
quotes.plain: What matters is inside you. You do not need luck to have it.

quotes.text: Despise poverty; no man lives as poor as he was born: despise pain; either it will cease or you will cease: despise death; it either ends you or takes you elsewhere: despise fortune; I have given her no weapon that can reach the mind.
quotes.plain: Poverty, pain, death and luck cannot touch your mind unless you let them.

quotes.text: Do you not blush to spend so long a time in dreading what takes so short a time to do?
quotes.plain: Dying takes seconds. You waste years afraid of it.

quotes.text: What then? Can heights be reached by a level path?
quotes.plain: Nothing great is reached on flat ground. The climb is the deal.

quotes.text: The wise man is safe, and no injury or insult can touch him.
quotes.plain: If you hold your own mind, other people's attacks cannot reach you.

quotes.text: The invulnerable is not that which is never struck, but that which is never wounded.
quotes.plain: Being strong means getting hit and staying unbroken, not never getting hit.

quotes.text: Now fortune does not give virtue; therefore she does not take it away.
quotes.plain: Luck can take your stuff but not your character, because luck never gave it to you.

quotes.text: Demetrius, who was surnamed Poliorcetes, took Megara, and the philosopher Stilbo, when asked by him whether he had lost anything, answered, “No, I carry all my property about me.”
quotes.plain: Lose everything and still own what counts: your mind and your standards.

quotes.text: Alone and elderly, and seeing everything around me in the hands of the enemy, still I declare that my property is whole and untouched.
quotes.plain: Even when the world takes everything, what's inside you can stay whole.

quotes.text: As for those fleeting possessions which change their owners, I know not where they are; what belongs to myself is with me, and ever will be.
quotes.plain: Stuff changes hands. What you built in yourself stays.

quotes.text: O! what laughter is to be got out of such things, with what amusement the mind may be filled when it contrasts the frantic follies of others with its own peace!
quotes.plain: Other people's drama gets funny once you're calm.

quotes.text: He who strives with a man makes himself that man’s rival, and must be on equal terms with him before he can overcome him.
quotes.plain: Fighting someone drags you down to their level first.

quotes.text: He does not regard what all men think low or wretched; he does not follow the people’s track, but as the stars move in a path opposite to that of the earth, so he proceeds contrary to the prejudices of all.
quotes.plain: Don't take your values from the crowd. Go your own direction.

quotes.text: The reproach of poverty agonizes some men, and whoever conceals it makes it a reproach to himself; and therefore if you of your own accord are the first to acknowledge it, you cut the ground from under the feet of those who would sneer and politely insult you; no one is laughed at who begins by laughing at himself.
quotes.plain: Own your flaws first and nobody can use them against you.

quotes.text: The nobler a man is by birth, by reputation, or by inheritance, the more bravely he should bear himself, remembering that the tallest men stand in the front rank in battle.
quotes.plain: The higher you climb, the more you get shot at. Stand up straight anyway.

quotes.text: Even though you be hard pressed and violently attacked by the enemy, still it is base to give way; hold the post assigned to you by nature.
quotes.plain: Don't quit your post just because it got hard.

quotes.text: Other vices can be concealed and cherished in secret; anger shows itself openly and appears in the countenance, and the greater it is, the more plainly it boils forth.
quotes.plain: Anger can't hide. Everyone sees it on your face.

quotes.text: Mankind is born for mutual assistance, anger for mutual ruin: the former loves society, the latter estrangement.
quotes.plain: People are built to help each other. Anger only wrecks things.

quotes.text: In the first place, it is easier to banish dangerous passions than to rule them; it is easier not to admit them than to keep them in order when admitted; for when they have established themselves in possession of the mind they are more powerful than the lawful ruler, and will in no wise permit themselves to be weakened or abridged.
quotes.plain: Easier to never start the bad habit than to manage it once it's in.

quotes.text: There are certain things whose beginnings lie in our own power, but which, when developed, drag us along by their own force and leave us no retreat.
quotes.plain: You can stop it at the start. Later it runs you.

quotes.text: Are you not ashamed to put virtues under the patronage of vices?
quotes.plain: Don't use your worst habits as the fuel for your best work.

quotes.text: By what did Fabius restore the shattered forces of the state, except by knowing how to delay and spin out time, which angry men know not how to do?
quotes.plain: Patience wins wars. Angry people can't wait.

quotes.text: Anger, therefore, is not useful even in wars or battles: for it is prone to rashness, and while trying to bring others into danger, does not guard itself against danger.
quotes.plain: Angry people get sloppy and hurt themselves.

quotes.text: The most trustworthy virtue is that which long and carefully considers itself, controls itself, and slowly and deliberately brings itself to the front.
quotes.plain: Real strength is slow, controlled and deliberate.

quotes.text: No man becomes braver through anger, except one who without anger would not have been brave at all: anger does not therefore come to assist courage, but to take its place.
quotes.plain: Rage is fake courage. Real courage doesn't need it.

quotes.text: Every weakling is naturally prone to complaint.
quotes.plain: Complaining is what weak people do.

quotes.text: No one, I affirm, will be found who can acquit himself.
quotes.plain: Nobody is clean. Remember that before you judge.

quotes.text: When a man is wandering about our fields because he has lost his way, it is better to place him on the right path than to drive him away.
quotes.plain: Someone who's lost needs directions, not a fight.

quotes.text: Nothing becomes one who inflicts punishment less than anger, because the punishment has all the more power to work reformation if the sentence be pronounced with deliberate judgment.
quotes.plain: Correct people calmly and it actually sticks.

quotes.text: Who can boast that he has his passions, under control, when Socrates did not dare to trust himself to his anger?
quotes.plain: If Socrates didn't trust himself angry, you shouldn't either.

quotes.text: O, how clever is anger at inventing reasons for its frenzy!
quotes.plain: Anger always finds a good excuse for itself.

quotes.text: The sword of justice is ill-placed in the hands of an angry man.
quotes.plain: Never make big decisions while furious.

quotes.text: Virtue alone is lofty and sublime, nor is anything great which is not at the same time tranquil.
quotes.plain: Real greatness is calm.

quotes.text: Among the other misfortunes of humanity is this, that men’s intellects are confused, and they not only cannot help going wrong, but love to go wrong.
quotes.plain: People mess up and often like it. Expect it.

quotes.text: To avoid being angry with individuals, you must pardon the whole mass, you must grant forgiveness to the entire human race.
quotes.plain: Lower your expectations of people and the anger shrinks.

quotes.text: Everything ought either to move us to tears or to laughter.
quotes.plain: Life is either sad or funny. Pick laughing.

quotes.text: We need a long-breathed struggle against permanent and prolific evils; not, indeed, to quell them, but merely to prevent their overpowering us.
quotes.plain: Some fights never end. The goal is to not get overrun.

quotes.text: He must fear many, whom so many fear.
quotes.plain: If you rule by fear, you live in it.

quotes.text: Whatever is a terror to others, fears for itself.
quotes.plain: Scary things are scared themselves.

quotes.text: Yet there is nothing so hard and difficult that the mind of man cannot overcome it, and with which unremitting study will not render him familiar, nor are there any passions so fierce and independent that they cannot be tamed by discipline.
quotes.plain: Nothing is too hard once you train at it. Even your worst temper.

quotes.text: What is more restful than a mind at peace, and what more toilsome than anger?
quotes.plain: Anger is exhausting. Calm is rest.

quotes.text: Modesty keeps holiday while vice is overwhelmed with work.
quotes.plain: The vice-ridden life is busy and tiring. The calm life rests.

quotes.text: Nor is it difficult to conquer our spirit, seeing that athletes, who devote their whole attention to the basest parts of themselves, nevertheless are able to endure blows and pain, in order to exhaust the strength of the striker, and do not strike when anger bids them, but when opportunity invites them.
quotes.plain: Fighters wait for the opening instead of swinging mad. You can do the same.

quotes.text: A man ought to be neither robber nor victim, neither tender-hearted nor cruel.
quotes.plain: Don't prey on people and don't be prey. Stay balanced.

quotes.text: Let the wise man be moderate, and when things have to be done somewhat briskly, let him call force, not anger, to his aid.
quotes.plain: Use force when needed. Don't use rage.

quotes.text: He to whom nothing is ever denied, will not be able to endure a rebuff, whose anxious mother always wipes away his tears, whose paedagogus is made to pay for his shortcomings.
quotes.plain: Get everything handed to you and you can't take a single no.

quotes.text: We should always allow some time to elapse, for time discloses the truth.
quotes.plain: Wait. The truth shows up with time.

quotes.text: We ought, therefore, to plead the cause of the absent against ourselves, and to keep our anger in abeyance: for a punishment which has been postponed may yet be inflicted, but when once inflicted cannot be recalled.
quotes.plain: You can still hit back tomorrow. You can't un-hit.

quotes.text: Readiness to believe what we hear causes very great mischief; we ought often not even to listen, because in some cases it is better to be deceived than to suspect deceit.
quotes.plain: Don't believe every rumor. Sometimes not knowing is better.

quotes.text: Suspicion will never lack grounds: what we want is straightforwardness, and a kindly interpretation of things.
quotes.plain: You can always find a reason to be suspicious. Choose the kind reading.

quotes.text: Nothing, therefore, nourishes anger more than excessive and dissatisfied luxury: the mind ought to be hardened by rough treatment, so as not to feel any blow that is not severe.
quotes.plain: Comfort makes you fragile and angry. Hardship toughens you.

quotes.text: Suppose that we are being punished; let us think not only of what we suffer, but of what we have done: let us sit in judgement on our past life.
quotes.plain: When it hurts, ask what you did to cause it.

quotes.text: A great part of mankind is not angry with sins, but with sinners.
quotes.plain: People hate the person more than the wrong.

quotes.text: The greatest remedy for anger is delay: beg anger to grant you this at the first, not in order that it may pardon the offence, but that it may form a right judgment about it: if it delays, it will come to an end.
quotes.plain: Just wait. Anger fades if you give it time.

quotes.text: The man who will tell you nothing save in secret hardly tells you anything at all.
quotes.plain: Be careful with gossip from people who won't stand behind it.

quotes.text: What can be more unjust than to believe in secret, and to be angry openly?
quotes.plain: Don't judge on whispers and then explode in public.

quotes.text: Is it a good man who has wronged you? do not believe it: is it a bad one? do not be surprised at this; he will pay to some one else the penalty which he owes to you, indeed, by his sin he has already punished himself.
quotes.plain: Bad people are already paying. You don't need to collect.

quotes.text: Fabius was wont to say that the most shameful excuse a general could make was “I did not think.”
quotes.plain: "I didn't expect that" is a weak excuse. Plan for it.

quotes.text: When you are especially enjoying yourself, be especially on your guard: when everything seems to you to be peaceful, be sure that mischief is not absent, but only asleep.
quotes.plain: Calm stretches end. Stay ready when things feel easy.

quotes.text: Always believe that something will occur to offend you.
quotes.plain: Expect it and it won't shock you.

quotes.text: As all the limbs act in unison, because it is the interest of the whole body to keep each one of them safe, so men should spare one another, because they are born for society.
quotes.plain: We're one body. Hurting each other hurts everyone.

quotes.text: It is the part of a great mind to despise wrongs done to it; the most contemptuous form of revenge is not to deem one’s adversary worth taking vengeance upon.
quotes.plain: The best revenge is not caring enough to bother.

quotes.text: Many have taken small injuries much more seriously to heart than they need, by revenging them: that man is great and noble who like a large wild animal hears unmoved the tiny curs that bark at him.
quotes.plain: Let the small dogs bark. Keep walking.

quotes.text: The wrongs of the powerful must not only be borne, but borne with a cheerful countenance: they will repeat the wrong if they think they have inflicted it.
quotes.plain: When you can't fight, don't let them see it land.

quotes.text: Every one knows the saying of the old courtier, who, when some one asked him how he had achieved the rare distinction of living at court till he reached old age, replied, “By receiving wrongs and returning thanks for them.”
quotes.plain: Survival sometimes means swallowing it and smiling.

quotes.text: A contest with one’s equal is of uncertain issue, with one’s superior is folly, and with one’s inferior is contemptible.
quotes.plain: Fights are always bad math: risky, stupid or petty.

quotes.text: How can we gain more glory than by turning anger into friendship?
quotes.plain: Turning an enemy into a friend is the real win.

quotes.text: If any one is angry with you, meet his anger by returning benefits for it: a quarrel which is only taken up on one side falls to the ground: it takes two men to fight.
quotes.plain: No second fighter, no fight.

quotes.text: But suppose that there is an angry struggle on both sides, even then, he is the better man who first gives way; the winner is the real loser.
quotes.plain: In a petty fight, stepping back is the winning move.

quotes.text: Does any one wish to strike his enemy so hard, as to leave his own hand in the wound, and not to be able to recover his balance after the blow? yet such a weapon is anger: it is scarcely possible to draw it back.
quotes.plain: Anger leaves you stuck in the wound with no way to recover.

quotes.text: No passion bears a more troubled aspect: it befouls the fairest face, makes fierce the expression which before was peaceful.
quotes.plain: Anger makes you ugly to everyone, including yourself.

quotes.text: Other passions gain a footing in the mind by slow degrees: anger’s conquest is sudden and complete, and, moreover, it makes all other passions subservient to itself.
quotes.plain: Other urges creep in. Anger takes over in a second and then runs everything else.

quotes.text: The other vices move our minds; anger hurls them headlong.
quotes.plain: Most vices nudge you. Anger throws you.

quotes.text: There is no passion that is more frantic, more destructive to its own self; it is arrogant if successful, and frantic if it fails.
quotes.plain: Anger is cocky when it wins and frantic when it loses. It never comes out well.

quotes.text: Avarice scrapes together and amasses riches for some better man to use: anger spends money; few can indulge in it for nothing.
quotes.plain: Greed at least saves money. Rage burns it.

quotes.text: Anger brings grief to a father, divorce to a husband, hatred to a magistrate, failure to a candidate for office.
quotes.plain: Anger costs you your family, your standing and your shot at the thing you want.

quotes.text: It is worse than luxury, because luxury enjoys its own pleasure, while anger enjoys another’s pain.
quotes.plain: Indulgence feeds on your own pleasure. Rage feeds on someone else's pain.

quotes.text: As weapons rebound from a hard surface, and solid substances hurt those who strike them, so also no insult can make a really great mind sensible of its presence, being weaker than that against which it is aimed.
quotes.plain: Insults only stick to a mind that is softer than the insult.

quotes.text: How far more glorious is it to throw back all wrongs and insults from oneself, like one wearing armour of proof against all weapons, for revenge is an admission that we have been hurt.
quotes.plain: Hitting back proves the insult landed. Let it bounce off instead.

quotes.text: That cannot be a great mind which is disturbed by injury.
quotes.plain: Being rattled by a slight shows how small the mind is.

quotes.text: He who has hurt you must be either stronger or weaker than yourself. If he be weaker, spare him: if he be stronger, spare yourself.
quotes.plain: If they are weaker, go easy on them. If they are stronger, protect yourself. Either way, skip the fight.

quotes.text: There is no greater proof of magnanimity than that nothing which befalls you should be able to move you to anger.
quotes.plain: Real strength is being unmoved by whatever happens to you.

quotes.text: We shall find much profit in that sound maxim of Democritus which defines peace of mind to consist in not labouring much, or too much for our strength, either in public or private matters.
quotes.plain: Peace of mind comes from not taking on more than you can carry.

quotes.text: Whenever you would attempt anything, first form an estimate both of your own powers, of the extent of the matter which you are undertaking, and of the means by which you are to accomplish it: for if you have to abandon your work when it is half done, the disappointment will sour your temper.
quotes.plain: Size up the job and your tools before you start, or quitting halfway will sour you.

quotes.text: Let our undertakings, therefore, be neither petty nor yet presumptuous and reckless: let our hopes not range far from home: let us attempt nothing which if we succeed will make us astonished at our success.
quotes.plain: Aim high, but not so high that success would shock you.

quotes.text: A dispute nourishes itself as it proceeds, and takes hold of those who plunge too deeply into it: it is easier to stand aloof than to extricate oneself from a struggle.
quotes.plain: Arguments feed themselves. Stay out of them early because getting out later is hard.

quotes.text: It is useful for a man to understand his disease, and to break its strength before it becomes developed.
quotes.plain: Know your own weakness and catch it while it is still small.

quotes.text: People do not all take offence in the same way; you ought then to know what your own weak point is, that you may guard it with especial care.
quotes.plain: Everyone has a trigger. Find yours and guard it.

quotes.text: Would you not be irascible? then be not inquisitive.
quotes.plain: If you don't want to be angry, stop digging for what people say about you.

quotes.text: A large part of mankind manufacture their own grievances either by entertaining unfounded suspicions or by exaggerating trifles.
quotes.plain: Most of our grievances are ones we built ourselves out of guesses and small stuff.

quotes.text: Anger often comes to us, but we often go to it. It ought never to be sent for: even when it falls in our way it ought to be flung aside.
quotes.plain: Anger finds you sometimes, but mostly you walk to it. Don't go looking.

quotes.text: If you want to find out the truth about anything, commit the task to time: nothing can be accurately discerned at a time of disturbance.
quotes.plain: You can't see clearly while you're worked up. Give it time first.

quotes.text: While you are angry, you ought not to be allowed to do anything.
quotes.plain: Don't act while you're angry. Not one thing.

quotes.text: Fight hard with yourself and if you cannot conquer anger, do not let it conquer you: you have begun to get the better of it if it does not show itself, if it is not given vent.
quotes.plain: If you can't kill the anger, at least don't let it out. Not showing it is the first win.

quotes.text: Our inward thoughts gradually become influenced by our outward demeanour.
quotes.plain: Act calm and the mind follows.

quotes.text: No yoke is so grievous as not to hurt him who struggles against it more than him who yields to it: the only way to alleviate great evils is to endure them and to submit to do what they compel.
quotes.plain: Fighting a burden hurts more than carrying it. Stop struggling and the weight eases.

quotes.text: The man who is not angry remains unshaken by injury: he who is angry has been moved by it.
quotes.plain: Staying calm shows you weren't moved. Anger shows you were.

quotes.text: You say, “I cannot endure it: injuries are hard to bear.” You lie; for how can any one not be able to bear injury, if he can bear to be angry?
quotes.plain: If you can stand being furious, you can stand the insult. It's the easier of the two.

quotes.text: Let us therefore be more gentle one to another: we are bad men, living among bad men: there is only one thing which can afford us peace, and that is to agree to forgive one another.
quotes.plain: Everyone is flawed. The only way to peace is to forgive each other.

quotes.text: How far better is it to heal an injury than to avenge it? Revenge takes up much time, and throws itself in the way of many injuries while it is smarting under one.
quotes.plain: Revenge eats time and invites more trouble. Healing is cheaper.

quotes.text: We all retain our anger longer than we feel our hurt: how far better it were to take the opposite course and not meet one mischief by another.
quotes.plain: The hurt fades faster than the grudge. Don't answer one mess with another.

quotes.text: A man will never be well off to whom it is a torture to see any one better off than himself.
quotes.plain: If someone else's success hurts you, you will never feel like you have enough.

quotes.text: Have I less than I hoped for? well, perhaps I hoped for more than I ought.
quotes.plain: Feeling shorted? Maybe you expected too much.

quotes.text: Do you ask, what is your greatest fault? It is, that you keep your accounts wrongly: you set a high value upon what you give, and a low one upon what you receive.
quotes.plain: You overvalue what you give and undervalue what you get.

quotes.text: Believe me, the things which cause us such great heat are trifles, the sort of things that children fight and squabble over: there is nothing serious, nothing important in all that we do with such gloomy faces.
quotes.plain: Most of what we fight over is kid stuff. Lighten up.

quotes.text: A narrow path causes quarrels among those who pass up and down it; a wide and broadly spread road may be used by whole tribes without jostling.
quotes.plain: Fight over small scraps and you clash. Aim at something wide and there's room for everyone.

quotes.text: What bad habit of yours have you cured to-day? what vice have you checked? in what respect are you better?
quotes.plain: Ask it every night: what did I fix, what did I resist, how am I better?

quotes.text: A good man delights in receiving advice: all the worst men are the most impatient of guidance.
quotes.plain: Good people want feedback. Fools hate it.

quotes.text: The mind is strong enough to bear those evils for which it is prepared.
quotes.plain: You can handle what you saw coming. So expect trouble.

quotes.text: To reprove a man when he is angry is to add to his anger by being angry oneself.
quotes.plain: Yelling at an angry person just doubles the fire.

quotes.text: Let us set our own conscience fully at rest, but make no efforts to gain credit for ourselves: so long as we deserve well, let us be satisfied, even if we should be ill spoken of.
quotes.plain: Live clean, do good work, and let them talk.

quotes.text: Let us not moderate anger, but get rid of it altogether: what can moderation have to do with an evil habit?
quotes.plain: Don't manage a bad habit. Cut it out.

quotes.text: Life is a matter which does not admit of waste, and we have no spare time to throw away.
quotes.plain: Life can't be wasted. There's no spare time.

quotes.text: The time which you have marked for the death of another perhaps includes your own.
quotes.plain: The day you wish on your enemy may cover you too.

quotes.text: Wait but a little while. See, here comes death, who will make you all equals.
quotes.plain: Death levels everyone soon enough. Hold on.

quotes.text: Let us keep our tempers in spite of losses, wrongs, abuse or sarcasm, and let us endure with magnanimity our shortlived troubles: while we are considering what is due to ourselves, as the saying is, and worrying ourselves, death will be upon us.
quotes.plain: Stay level through losses and slights. Death is closing in while you stew.

quotes.text: Nothing, therefore, is more important than that we should not, like sheep, follow the flock that has gone before us, and thus proceed not whither we ought, but whither the rest are going.
quotes.plain: Don't follow the herd just because it's moving. Pick your own direction.

quotes.text: Let us therefore inquire, not what is most commonly done, but what is best for us to do, and what will establish us in the possession of undying happiness, not what is approved of by the vulgar, the worst possible exponents of truth.
quotes.plain: Do what is best, not what is popular. The crowd is a bad judge.

quotes.text: The happy man, therefore, is he who can make a right judgment in all things: he is happy who in his present circumstances, whatever they may be, is satisfied and on friendly terms with the conditions of his life.
quotes.plain: Happy means seeing clearly and being at peace with where you are.

quotes.text: A man should be unbiassed and not to be conquered by external things: he ought to admire himself alone, to feel confidence in his own spirit, and so to order his life as to be ready alike for good or for bad fortune.
quotes.plain: Trust yourself and stay ready for good luck or bad.

quotes.text: You may, then, boldly declare that the highest good is singleness of mind: for where agreement and unity are, there must the virtues be: it is the vices that are at war one with another.
quotes.plain: Being whole, with no inner war, is the goal.

quotes.text: Why do you talk of pleasures to me? I am seeking to find what is good for man, not for his belly; why, cattle and whales have larger ones than he.
quotes.plain: I want what's good for a person, not for his stomach. Cattle have bigger ones.

quotes.text: You devote yourself to pleasures, I check them; you indulge in pleasure, I use it; you think that it is the highest good, I do not even think it to be good: for the sake of pleasure I do nothing, you do everything.
quotes.plain: You chase pleasure. I keep it on a leash.

quotes.text: Let virtue lead the way and bear the standard: we shall have pleasure for all that, but we shall be her masters and controllers; she may win some concessions from us, but will not force us to do anything.
quotes.plain: Enjoy things, but on your terms. Pleasure takes orders, not gives them.

quotes.text: You do not afford virtue a solid immoveable base if you bid it stand on what is unsteady: and what can be so unsteady as dependence on mere chance, and the vicissitudes of the body and of those things which act on the body?
quotes.plain: Build on what you control, not luck or your body's moods.

quotes.text: Let us bear with magnanimity whatever the system of the universe makes it needful for us to bear: we are all bound by this oath: “To bear the ills of mortal life, and to submit with a good grace to what we cannot avoid.”
quotes.plain: Accept what you can't avoid with grace.

quotes.text: I am not a wise man, and I will not be one in order to feed your spite: so do not require me to be on a level with the best of men, but merely to be better than the worst: I am satisfied, if every day I take away something from my vices and correct my faults.
quotes.plain: Don't expect perfect. Just be a little better each day than the worst, and keep trimming.

quotes.text: I’ve lived, I’ve run the race which Fortune set me.
quotes.plain: Finish your race so you can say this at the end.

quotes.text: Men deserve praise for engaging in profitable studies, even though they stop short of producing any results.
quotes.plain: Trying to learn and improve counts, even if it doesn't pay off yet.

quotes.text: I will do nothing because of public opinion, but everything because of conscience: whenever I do anything alone by myself I will believe that the eyes of the Roman people are upon me while I do it.
quotes.plain: Act as if watched even when alone, and answer to your conscience rather than the crowd.

quotes.text: So croak away, and exercise your miserable tongues in reproaching good men: open wide your jaws, bite hard: you will break many teeth before you make any impression.
quotes.plain: Haters wear themselves out on you. Let them bite.

quotes.text: In fine, my riches belong to me, you belong to your riches.
quotes.plain: Own your stuff or it owns you.

quotes.text: As he is capable of performing a journey upon his own feet, but yet would prefer to mount a carriage, just so he will be capable of being poor, yet will wish to be rich; he will own wealth, but will view it as an uncertain possession which will some day fly away from him.
quotes.plain: You can be fine without money, enjoy it when you have it, and know it can vanish.

quotes.text: All the difference in the world: for riches are slaves in the house of a wise man, but masters in that of a fool.
quotes.plain: Money serves the wise and masters the fool.

quotes.text: The hardness of flint is known to none so well as to those who strike it.
quotes.plain: Whoever attacks you learns how hard you are.

quotes.text: I offer myself to all attacks, like some lonely rock in a shallow sea, which the waves never cease to beat upon from whatever quarter they may come, but which they cannot thereby move from its place nor yet wear away, for however many years they may unceasingly dash against it.
quotes.plain: Be the rock in the waves. Hits don't move you.

quotes.text: The duty of a man is to be useful to his fellow-men; if possible, to be useful to many of them; failing this, to be useful to a few; failing this, to be useful to his neighbours, and, failing them, to himself: for when he helps others, he advances the general interests of mankind.
quotes.plain: Be useful to as many people as you can. If you can't reach many, reach a few. Start small and still count.

quotes.text: Who dares to tell himself the truth?
quotes.plain: Almost nobody. The first lie you hear is your own.

quotes.text: Who is there, by however large a troop of caressing courtiers he may be surrounded, who in spite of them is not his own greatest flatterer?
quotes.plain: Your own flattery does more damage than anyone else's. You are the biggest yes-man you have.

quotes.text: What you desire, to be undisturbed, is a great thing, nay, the greatest thing of all, and one which raises a man almost to the level of a god.
quotes.plain: A calm mind is the biggest win there is. Chase it before you chase anything else.

quotes.text: We must understand, therefore, that what we suffer from is not the fault of the places but of ourselves: we are weak when there is anything to be endured, and cannot support either labour or pleasure, either one’s own business or any one else’s for long.
quotes.plain: Changing scenery won't fix it. The problem travels with you.

quotes.text: Neither should you engage in anything from which you are not free to retreat: apply yourself to something which you can finish, or at any rate can hope to finish: you had better not meddle with those operations which grow in importance, while they are being transacted, and which will not stop where you intended them to stop.
quotes.plain: Don't start what you can't finish or get out of. Watch for projects that keep growing past the size you planned.

quotes.text: We should choose for our friends men who are, as far as possible, free from strong desires: for vices are contagious, and pass from a man to his neighbour, and injure those who touch them.
quotes.plain: You pick up the habits of the people around you. Choose friends who aren't run by their appetites.

quotes.text: Above all, however, avoid dismal men who grumble at whatever happens, and find something to complain of in everything.
quotes.plain: Stay away from chronic complainers. Their mood becomes yours.

quotes.text: Diogenes, a man of infinite spirit, perceived this, and made it impossible that anything should be taken from him.
quotes.plain: Diogenes owned so little that nothing could be taken. You can't be robbed of what you never leaned on.

quotes.text: Are you not ashamed of yourself, you who gaze upon riches with astonished admiration?
quotes.plain: Staring at other people's money with wide eyes is beneath you.

quotes.text: Look upon the universe: you will see the gods quite bare of property, and possessing nothing though they give everything.
quotes.plain: The most powerful things you can picture own nothing. Owning stuff isn't what makes something great.

quotes.text: How far happier is he who is indebted to no man for anything except for what he can deprive himself of with the greatest ease!
quotes.plain: The freest person owes nothing he can't easily give up.

quotes.text: Let us then teach ourselves to be able to dine without all Rome to look on, to be the slaves of fewer slaves, to get clothes which fulfil their original purpose, and to live in a smaller house.
quotes.plain: Train yourself to live simpler and without an audience. Less stuff, fewer people to answer to.

quotes.text: What is the use of possessing numberless books and libraries, whose titles their owner can hardly read through in a lifetime?
quotes.plain: A huge pile you never use is just decoration. Own what you actually read.

quotes.text: A student is overwhelmed by such a mass, not instructed, and it is much better to devote yourself to a few writers than to skim through many.
quotes.plain: Go deep on a few sources instead of skimming a hundred.

quotes.text: Let a man, then, obtain as many books as he wants, but none for show.
quotes.plain: Buy what you will use. Don't buy to look like you read.

quotes.text: Knowing to what sorrows we were born, there is nothing for which Nature more deserves our thanks than for having invented habit as an alleviation of misfortune, which soon accustoms us to the severest evils.
quotes.plain: Habit is a mercy. Hard things get easier because you get used to them.

quotes.text: No one could hold out against misfortune if it permanently exercised the same force as at its first onset.
quotes.plain: The first hit is always the worst. It never lands that hard again.

quotes.text: We are all chained to Fortune: some men’s chain is loose and made of gold, that of others is tight and of meaner metal: but what difference does this make?
quotes.plain: Rich or poor, everybody is tied to something. The chain's material matters less than you think.

quotes.text: All life is slavery: let each man therefore reconcile himself to his lot, complain of it as little as possible, and lay hold of whatever good lies within his reach.
quotes.plain: Everyone is stuck with something. Complain less and grab the good that is in reach.

quotes.text: No condition can be so wretched that an impartial mind can find no compensations in it.
quotes.plain: There is something to gain even in the worst spot, if you look fairly.

quotes.text: Call good sense to your aid against difficulties: it is possible to soften what is harsh, to widen what is too narrow, and to make heavy burdens press less severely upon one who bears them skilfully.
quotes.plain: Clear thinking makes a hard load lighter. How you carry it changes how heavy it is.

quotes.text: Neither let us envy those who are in high places: the heights which look lofty to us are steep and rugged.
quotes.plain: The top looks great from below. It's steep and dangerous up there.

quotes.text: Disease, captivity, disaster, conflagration, are none of them unexpected: I always knew with what disorderly company Nature had associated me.
quotes.plain: Bad things aren't a shock if you knew the deal when you signed up.

quotes.text: How large a part of mankind never think of storms when about to set sail?
quotes.plain: Most people head out to sea without once picturing a storm.

quotes.text: It is too late to school the mind to endurance of peril after peril has come.
quotes.plain: Build toughness before the hit. Once it lands, it's too late to start.

quotes.text: Where are the riches after which want, hunger, and beggary do not follow?
quotes.plain: Any fortune can be lost. Nothing you own is safe from falling.

quotes.text: Know then that every station of life is transitory, and that what has ever happened to anybody may happen to you also.
quotes.plain: Whatever happened to anyone can happen to you. Nothing you hold is permanent.

quotes.text: Among such continual topsy-turvy changes, unless you expect that whatever can happen will happen to you, you give adversity power against you, a power which can be destroyed by any one who looks at it beforehand.
quotes.plain: Look straight at what could go wrong ahead of time and it loses its power over you.

quotes.text: They move uselessly and without any plan, just like ants crawling over bushes, which creep up to the top and then down to the bottom again without gaining anything.
quotes.plain: Motion isn't progress. You can crawl all day and end up exactly where you started.

quotes.text: I will set sail unless anything happens to prevent me, I shall be praetor, if nothing hinders me, my financial operations will succeed, unless anything goes wrong with them.
quotes.plain: Plan with a built-in escape clause. Then a setback never blindsides you.

quotes.text: Zeno, the chief of our school, when he heard the news of a shipwreck, in which all his property had been lost, remarked, “Fortune bids me follow philosophy in lighter marching order.”
quotes.plain: He lost everything and called it traveling lighter. Losing stuff can be a gift.

quotes.text: We must take a higher view of all things, and bear with them more easily: it better becomes a man to scoff at life than to lament over it.
quotes.plain: Laugh at the mess instead of crying over it. It's easier to carry.

quotes.text: So deeply has this evil of being guided by the opinion of others taken root in us, that even grief, the simplest of all emotions, begins to be counterfeited.
quotes.plain: We fake even our sadness for the crowd. That's how deep other people's opinion runs.

quotes.text: I will never weep for a man who dies cheerfully, nor for one who dies weeping: the former wipes away my tears, the latter by his tears makes himself unworthy that any should be shed for him.
quotes.plain: How you face the end decides whether anyone needs to mourn you.

quotes.text: Men’s minds ought to have relaxation: they rise up better and more vigorous after rest.
quotes.plain: Rest is part of the work. You come back sharper.

quotes.text: There is a great difference between slackening your hold of a thing and letting it go.
quotes.plain: Easing off for a day is not quitting. Know which one you are doing.

quotes.text: “We live a small part only of our lives.”
