quotes.plain: Most of your days barely count as lived.

quotes.text: You cannot find any one who wants to distribute his money; yet among how many people does every one distribute his life?
quotes.plain: Nobody hands out cash to strangers, but everyone gives their time away for free.

quotes.text: You fear everything, like mortals as you are, and yet you desire everything as if you were immortals.
quotes.plain: You're scared like you'll die and greedy like you won't.

quotes.text: How late it is to begin life just when we have to be leaving it!
quotes.plain: Don't wait until the end to start living.

quotes.text: What a foolish forgetfulness of our mortality, to put off wholesome counsels until our fiftieth or sixtieth year, and to choose that our lives shall begin at a point which few of us ever reach.
quotes.plain: Putting off the good life until later bets on a date most people never reach.

quotes.text: Cicero called himself “half a prisoner,” but, by Hercules, the wise man never would have come under so lowly a title: he never would be half a prisoner, but would always enjoy complete and entire liberty, being free, in his own power, and greater than all others: for what can be greater than the man who is greater than Fortune?
quotes.plain: A wise person is never even half a prisoner. Staying above Fortune is real greatness.

quotes.text: No man knows less about living than a business man: there is nothing about which it is more difficult to gain knowledge.
quotes.plain: Being busy doesn't teach you how to live. It may teach you less than anything.

quotes.text: Balance your account, and run over all the days of your life; you will see that only a very few days, and only those which were useless for any other purpose, have been left to you.
quotes.plain: Add up your days. Very few were actually yours.

quotes.text: You have no grounds, therefore, for supposing that any one has lived long, because he has wrinkles or grey hairs: such a man has not lived long, but has only been long alive.
quotes.plain: Old doesn't mean lived. Surviving a long time isn't the same as using it.

quotes.text: Yet it is easy to arrange the distribution of a quantity, however small, if we know how much there is: what you ought to husband most carefully is that which may run short you know not when.
quotes.plain: Guard hardest what can run out without warning. Your time is that.

quotes.text: You dispose of that which is in the hand of Fortune, and you let go that which is in your own.
quotes.plain: You gamble with what you can't control and drop what you can.

quotes.text: Whither are you looking, whither are you stretching forward? everything future is uncertain: live now straightway.
quotes.plain: The future isn't guaranteed. Start living today.

quotes.text: Our swiftness in making use of our time ought therefore to vie with the swiftness of time itself, and we ought to drink of it as we should of a fast-running torrent which will not be always running.
quotes.plain: Move as fast as time does. Drink while the river is running.

quotes.text: No one, unless all his acts have been submitted to the infallible censorship of his own conscience, willingly turns his thoughts back upon the past.
quotes.plain: People avoid looking back when they don't like what they'd see. Live so you can look.

quotes.text: O, how doth excessive prosperity blind our intellects!
quotes.plain: Too much success makes you stupid.

quotes.text: Since Nature allows us to commune with every age, why do we not abstract ourselves from our own petty fleeting span of time, and give ourselves up with our whole mind to what is vast, what is eternal, what we share with better men than ourselves?
quotes.plain: Read the great minds of every age. You can spend time with the best people who ever lived.

quotes.text: Those men lead the shortest and unhappiest lives who forget the past, neglect the present, and dread the future: when they reach the end of it the poor wretches learn too late that they were busied all the while that they were doing nothing.
quotes.plain: Forget the past, ignore today, fear tomorrow, and you end up busy and empty.

quotes.text: Everything for which we are dependent on chance is uncertain: the higher it rises, the more opportunities it has of falling.
quotes.plain: The higher you rise on luck, the further there is to fall.

quotes.text: We shall never lack causes of anxiety, either pleasurable or painful: our life will be pushed along from one business to another: leisure will always be wished for, and never enjoyed.
quotes.plain: There's always one more thing, and rest keeps getting pushed back.

quotes.text: When, therefore, you see a man often wear the purple robes of office, and hear his name often repeated in the forum, do not envy him: he gains these things by losing so much of his life.
quotes.plain: Don't envy the famous. They paid with their time.
